title: Simon Critchley at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Simon Critchley —Hans Jonas Professor of Philosophy at the New School for Social Research in New York—for a discussion of his new book, Heidegger Thinking: ‘Being and Time’ Explained. He will be joined in conversation by Sean Kelly —Dean of Arts and Humanities and Teresa G. and Ferdinand F. Martignetti Professor of Philosophy at Harvard University. About Heidegger Thinking An intelligent but approachable guide to the main concepts of Heidegger’s magnum opus, Being and Time , by one of the leading philosophers of our day. Heidegger Thinking: ‘ Being and Time ‘ Explained is a comprehensive, long-form deep dive into what is arguably the most significant philosophical work of the last century. Scheduled for release ahead of the 2027 centenary of Heidegger’s masterpiece, this volume by Simon Critchley (edited by Ben Olson) aims to explain the entirety of Heidegger’s project in terms that are understandable and—most importantly—usable for intelligent, curious laypeople. The book is structured into 18 chapters, each presenting a key concept such as Dasein, Being-in-the-world, Anxiety, and Ecstatic Temporality. Critchley avoids the “bazaar of pop philosophy,” opting instead for a slow, intimate journey through Heidegger’s notoriously difficult architecture without sacrificing depth. The work originated as a popular podcast series recorded during the 2020 pandemic, capturing a cultural moment where themes of mortality and isolation were uniquely resonant. However, this text is a complete rewrite, clarified and expanded with a full scholarly apparatus for independent study. Critchley’s central thesis is that “Being is time and time is finite.” By stripping away Heidegger’s baroque jargon, he demonstrates how Heidegger’s insights into our “thrown open clearing of finitude” can change one’s life. This book invites readers to master the “rhythm of existence” and move beyond the “cabinet of consciousness” to embrace a lived, worldly experience. Heidegg

title: Mouths of Babes
description: Mouths of Babes is an award-winning folk-Americana duo known for smart songwriting, tight vocal harmonies, and a rare, intimate connection with their audience. Their band motto, “All the feelings, all the time” is no joke; at shows, fans snort with laughter, cry into their date’s shoulder, and make confessions at the merch table. Fronted by veteran performers Ty Greenstein and Ingrid Elizabeth, the duo delivers the kind of emotionally rich lyricism and disarming humor that keeps audiences leaning forward in their seats from first note to encore. Both artists come from acclaimed musical lineages and storied careers. Before forming Mouths of Babes, Ty and Ingrid toured nationally for years with their respective bands, Girlyman and Coyote Grace, sharing the stage with artists like Dar Williams, Melissa Ferrick, and the Indigo Girls and quickly becoming headliners themselves. The two singer-songwriters met on tour, and when both bands split up around the same time, they didn’t hesitate before combining forces. Now they have distilled the best of the songwriting, musicianship, and humor of their previous groups into what the Huffington Post calls “powerful, romantic, and giddy…a musical and personal love fest all at once.” Onstage, Ingrid and Ty trade lead vocals, instruments, and jokes with ease—Ty on guitars, banjo, and foot percussion; Ingrid on upright bass, ukulele, harmonica, and cajón—seamlessly creating a show that can span a dizzying range of genres: singer-songwriter, blues, soul, folk-rock, country, even musical theater. Beyond the stage, Mouths of Babes is known for cultivating genuine community. From wildly successful fan-funded albums to their pandemic-era online concert series Live From the Baberhood, the duo has built a devoted following rooted in connection and care. As Café Veritas wrote: “This is the kind of music that makes you glad to be alive.”

As a comedian, Bobcat has starred in numerous HBO/Showtime specials, performed in venues worldwide, and even went on tour as an opening act for the band Nirvana. Well-known for his roles in “Scrooged” with Bill Murray and as Zed in the “Police Academy” franchise, Goldthwait has become a well-respected Award- Winning Director, too. His directorial works include feature films World’s Greatest Dad, starring Robin Williams, Willow Creek, starring Bigfoot, God Bless America, Windy City Heat, Sleeping Dogs Lie, and the documentaries Call Me Lucky and Joy Ride. In addition to being a 4x Sundance Alumni, Goldthwait’s films have played internationally, including the Deauville Film Festival and San Sebastian Film Festival. Bobcat has been honored with the German Independent Honorary Award at the Oldenburg Film Festival for his collective works and was awarded “Filmmaker on the Edge” at the Provincetown Film Festival by his hero John Waters. His TV direction includes his series, Misfits and Monsters, Jimmy Kimmel Live, Community, Maron, Those Who Can’t, and many more. Goldthwait has directed numerous standup comedy specials for folks like Patton Oswalt, Marc Maron, Ron Funches, Kyle Kinane, Cameron Esposito, Mo Willems, Gary Gulman, Hari Kondabolu, Eugene Mirman, and Pete Davidson to name a few. Comedian Bobcat Goldthwait first appeared on the David Letterman Show at the age of 20 and has an ongoing career as a writer, director, actor, voice actor, and stand-up. As a comedian, Bobcat has starred in numerous HBO/Showtime specials, performed in venues worldwide, and even went on tour as an opening act for the band Nirvana. Well-known for his roles in “Scrooged” with Bill Murray and as Zed in the “Police Academy” franchise, Goldthwait has become a well-respected Award- Winning Director, too. His directorial works include feature films World’s Greatest Dad, starring Robin Williams, Willow Creek, starring Bigfoot, God Bless America, Windy City Heat, Sleeping Dogs Lie, and the documentaries Call Me Lucky and Joy Ride. In addition to being a 4x Sundance Alumni, Goldthwait’s films have played internationally, including the Deauville Film Festival and San Sebastian Film Festival. Bobcat has been honored with the German Independent Honorary Award at the Oldenburg Film Festival for his collective works and was awarded “Filmmaker on the Edge” at the Provincetown Film Festival by his hero John Waters. His TV direction includes his series, Misfits and Monsters, Jimmy Kimmel Live, Community, Maron, Those Who Can’t, and many more. Goldthwait has directed numerous standup comedy specials for folks like Patton Oswalt, Marc Maron, Ron Funches, Kyle Kinane, Cameron Esposito, Mo Willems, Gary Gulman, Hari Kondabolu, Eugene Mirman, and Pete Davidson to name a few. Bobcat is currently working on several new film projects and has started his autobiography. title: Ira Klein & Liz Walker- A Music and Dance Celebration
description: Join former Artist-in-Residence Ira Klein and Liz Walker for a music and dance performance in Bigelow Chapel. Ira Klein (2022-2023 Artist-in-Residence) returns to Mount Auburn to celebrate music from his new record, Solo Guitar . His performance will include compositions inspired by historic oak trees on Mount Auburn’s grounds, as well as a variety of original and traditional Middle-Eastern music. Special guest dancer/choreographer Liz Walker (2022-2023 Artist-in-Residence) will join the stage to perform select pieces from At The Seam of Life and Death , Ira and Liz’s collaborative piece. Together, Walker and Klein playfully explore the beautiful acoustics and space of the majestic Bigelow Chapel, surrounding the audience with an immersive arts experience. Liz Walker is a classically trained ballet dancer and choreographer based in Cambridge. After completing her training at American Ballet Theatre’s school, she joined Los Angeles Ballet as an inaugural member in 2006. With Los Angeles Ballet she performed as a soloist, dancing a variety of roles in the classical, Balanchine, modern, and contemporary repertory. As a choreographer, Walker explores personal lived experience through movement. She uses dance as a vehicle for social commentary and change while emphasizing the medium’s strength as the embodiment of music. Walker was a 2022-2023 Artist-in-Residence at Mount Auburn Cemetery and has returned to Mount Auburn often to create and perform. She lives in Cambridge with her husband and two young children. Ira Klein is a Brooklyn based guitarist, composer, and educator. Specializing in Middle-Eastern music, American folk, and music for dance, he seamlessly combines a lifelong passion for musical traditions with a love of experimentation. In 2022-2023 Ira was an Artist-in-Residence at Mount Auburn Cemetery, where he created The Oak Cycle, a suite of instrumental guitar music dedicated to historic oak trees.

Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. Spotlight Tours are designed and led by Harvard undergraduates from a range of academic disciplines. Each tour is focused on objects chosen by the student and provides visitors a unique, thematic view into the collections. Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. Open to the public, these tours start outside the museum shop on Saturdays and Sundays at 11am and 2pm. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. The Ho Family Student Guide Program at the Harvard Art Museums prepares students to develop original, research-based tours. title: Jim Infantino, Terry Kitchen, Jack Byrne at McCarthy's Sunday Oct 11
description: Somerville Songwriter Sessions at McCarthy's presents singer/songwriters Jim Infantino, Terry Kitchen, and Jack Byrne on Sunday afternoon October 11. The show begins at 4:00 pm and admission is $15 in advance, $20 at the door. McCarthy's is at 1920 Mass. Ave, Cambridge, across from the Porter Square Red Line T station. For advance tickets visit https://tickets.24hourmusic.com/eventperformances.asp?evt=1866. For more information call McCarthy's at 617-945-1887, visit https://www.mccarthystoad.com/, or https://www.facebook.com/SomervilleSongwriterSessions or email SomervilleSongwriterSessions@gmail.com. Somerville Songwriter Sessions at McCarthy's presents contemporary folk singer/songwriters in concert on the second Sunday afternoon of each month. Each performer will do a solo set, followed by a round-robin with all three performers. McCarthy's features live music in a comfortable, listening room setting, and features a full menu and bar. Our 10/11 performers: Jim Infantino has been performing his own brand of off-kilter folk music since the '80s when he was an underage teen sneaking into Dave Van Ronk's open mic at The Speakeasy on Macdougal Street. His songs have been described as satirical, witty, sardonic, urbane, funny, heartbreaking, catchy, philosophical and razor sharp. Sometimes political, sometimes personal, sometimes abstract, his songs weave in the hint of humor when you expect sadness and tragedy when you expect levity. Since 1996 he has been performing both solo and with his band Jim's Big Ego, who describe themselves as "the greatest band in the history of recorded music." With the band he has released 7 full-length CDs adding to his 4 solo releases including his latest, 2025's Assemble Yourself. He is also a novelist, with his debut book The Wakeful Wanderer's Guide to New New England and Beyond winning the 2017 Wattys Newcomer's Award, and its sequel, The Wakeful Wanderer's Guide to Disillusionment, appearing in 2021. More on Jim at jiminfantino.co

title: Jerry Bergonzi Quartet
description: Jerry Bergonzi, Tenor Saxophone A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination, Jerry Bergonzi has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. — By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

description: Instructor: Rachel Mirus Price: $35 members / $40 nonmembers What makes a cluster of abstract shapes look like a tiger face? title: The Tobacco Takers: Puritans, Pipes, and Bodily Care
description: Free Hybrid Lecture Speakers: Diana DiPaolo Loren , Deputy Director for Curatorial Affairs and Senior Curator, Peabody Museum, Harvard University Stephen W. Silliman , Professor, Department of Anthropology, University of Massachusetts Boston Indigenous to the Americas and cultivated by Native peoples for thousands of years, tobacco was introduced to Europeans in the 16th century, and by the early 17th century, it had spread across the globe. In Puritan New England, religious leaders condemned tobacco as sinful while early practitioners used it as medicine. Clay tobacco pipes commonly found at 17th-century archaeological sites in Massachusetts reveal widespread use despite strict social and religious restrictions. Drawing from her new book, The Tobacco Takers: Puritanism, Smoking, Health, and the Archaeology of Bodily Care (Bloomsbury Publishing, 2026), Diana DiPaolo Loren will share archaeological, archival, and visual evidence that recasts tobacco and tobacco pipes as tools of bodily care for both physical and metaphysical ailments. The program will include a conversation with archaeologist Stephen W. Silliman. Copies of The Tobacco Takers will be available for purchase after the program. Advance registration is recommended for online and in-person attendance. Free event parking is available with registration at the 52 Oxford Street Garage , starting at 5:00 pm. Register by October 12th, 2026 to receive parking registration instructions. Presented by the Peabody Museum of Archaeology & Ethnology and the Harvard Museums of Science & Culture. About the Speakers Diana DiPaolo Loren (PhD, State University of New York at Binghamton) is Deputy Director for Curatorial Affairs and Senior Curator at the Peabody Museum of Archaeology and Ethnology, Harvard University. Loren specializes in the colonial northeastern United States, with a focus on the body, health, dress, and adornment. title: Pınar Öğrenci: Good Luck in Germany
description: The 2026 Busch-Reisinger Museum Lecture Berlin-based artist and filmmaker Pınar Öğrenci will discuss her 2024 film Glück auf in Deutschland (Good Luck in Germany), which is featured in her first major exhibition in the United States, here at the Harvard Art Museums. The film examines the construction of postwar German identity in the Ruhrgebiet, a heavily industrialized region known for coal mining and steel production, as shaped by layered experiences of survival, resistance, and resilience. In it, Öğrenci applies a feminist lens, broadening the history of industrial labor beyond the male worker and the factory. The lecture brings Glück auf in Deutschland into conversation with Öğrenci’s other films, exploring filmmaking as a political practice through which the history of “guest workers” can be connected to ongoing struggles around labor, migration, and belonging. The exhibition Pınar Öğrenci: Glück auf in Deutschland (April 16, 2026–October 18, 2026) includes the 2024 film Glück auf in Deutschland (Good Luck in Germany) as well as five related collages that reimagine the bodies of workers and their families within the Ruhr landscape and its architecture. Öğrenci’s use of the phrase Glück auf—a common way that miners wish one another a safe return after their physically grueling and dangerous work underground—resonates with the experiences of immigrant communities in present-day Germany facing right-wing extremism. Following the program, guests are invited to visit the exhibition on Level 1. This lecture will be recorded and made available for online viewing; check back shortly after the event for the link to view. This event is part of In Conversation, a series of evening programs that feature local and international curators, artists, scholars, and more. Running from September through April, these events highlight our temporary exhibitions, permanent collections, and a range of creative voices. title: SOLD OUT! Lectures On Tap: “Neuroscientist Explains: The Modules of the Mind”
description: Lectures On Tap: “Neuroscientist Explains: The Modules of the Mind” Event Description: 🎤 Speaker: Michael Cohen We tend to think of the brain as a general-purpose, endlessly adaptable supercomputer. In reality, it’s far stranger and more fascinating. The brain isn’t one big machine at all, but a collection of quirky specialists—distinct modules, each with its own narrow job and responsibilities. When one of these specialists goes offline due to stroke, accident, or disease, the results can be startling. Some people can no longer recognize faces, even their own. Others lose the ability to feel fear while every other emotion remains intact. Some can’t understand other people’s intentions, while others see their moral compass and personal values radically change. In this engaging talk, neuroscientist Michael Cohen will guide you on a tour of these hidden specialists in your head: the modules that let you recognize a smile, feel empathy, and navigate the social world. By the end, you’ll gain a clearer picture not only of how your brain is organized, but of the fundamental structures that shape your own mind. Michael Cohen is a Professor of Neuroscience and Psychology at Amherst College and a Research Scientist at MIT. title: Aruni Kashyap at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Aruni Kashyap —acclaimed author, translator, and an associate professor and director of the Creative Writing Program at the University of Georgia—for a discussion of his new novel, How to Date a Fanatic. He will be joined in conversation by Neel Mukherjee —award-winning author and Senior Lecturer in Creative Writing at Harvard University. About How to Date a Fanatic In this compassionate, poignant novel set-in contemporary India, a young professor searches for connection and love during a time of political and cultural upheaval. As political tensions rise precipitously across India, Rohit returns to Delhi University to teach and gets caught in a web of unrequited love with his friend Dhruv. To alleviate his inevitable heartbreak, Rohit seeks relationships with other men in the city, until he meets and embarks on a delicate new romance with the effervescent Sayan, a literature student he hopes will be the answer to getting over Dhruv. Rohit’s life soon becomes more complicated as the country’s political tensions erupt on campus, sparking a turbulent student-led movement that entangles Rohit when Dhruv joins the fray, a tipping point that changes Rohit’s life forever. Set against the vibrant, volatile tapestry of modern India, Rohit and his friends must learn to navigate the challenges and triumphs of queer life to survive in an unpredictable political landscape. Propulsive, tense, and charged with humor and tenderness, How to Date a Fanatic is an exploration of identity, connection, and the enduring hope for a better future in a rapidly changing world.

title: Bandits on the Run
description: Bandits on the Run are a musical trio from the Brooklyn-Queens border. Born from a chance encounter busking on the subway, Adrian Blake Enscoe, Sydney Shepherd, and Regina Strayhorn defy convention with an impressive trade-off of lead vocals and instruments. The Bandits marry acoustic, electric, and bass guitar sounds with cello, accordion, suitcases-turned-kickdrums, and (if you’re lucky) sometimes even a megaphone. The Bandit’s three-part harmonies have been heard filling iconic venues while opening for The Wood Brothers’ 2025 East Coast tour, on the main stages at Colorado’s Rocky Mount Folks Fest and Michigan’s Blissfest, and in a sold out residency at Manhattan’s Bowery Electric. Their songs have been featured by NPR’s Tiny Desk and The Moth Story Slam, as well as in Netflix’s Ask the StoryBots and the feature film The Same Storm. The Bandits tour nationally and internationally, with appearances at Cambridge Folk Festival, Floydfest, Summerfest Milwaukee, Americanafest, F1 Singapore Grand Prix, Mile of Music, and more. Their theatrical indie-folk lends itself quite well to storytelling and their work adapting text for a musical production of As You Like It later became their EP The Shakespeare Tapes. In addition to all their touring and recording work, Bandits on the Run are also in the business of writing musicals, sometimes as a trio and sometimes with collaborators. They are currently creating the stage musical adaptation of the novel What’s Eating Gilbert Grape with actor-musician-longtime friend Christopher Sears and newfound friend Academy Award Nominee Peter Hedges, supported by MCC Theater. Bandits on the Run are also developing an original musical, Yukon Ho, about a group of Black prospectors in the Alaskan gold rush, Yukon Ho was researched on the ground in Skagway, Alaska with support from the NEA, and has been workshopped with support from Prospect Musicals. They are alumni of several musical theater writing development programs, including Berkeley

description: Postpartum Movement is a welcoming, supportive space to move, reconnect, and care for yourself during the postpartum journey. Majestic Healing Pathways™ is the foundational care model that guides all of Majestic Community Wellness’s programs. It reflects our belief that healing is a right — not a privilege — and that healing happens most sustainably when care is consistent, culturally grounded, and rooted in community. Developed in response to gaps in traditional health and wellness systems, Majestic Healing Pathways™ centers the lived experiences of Black and Brown communities who face disproportionate stress, trauma, and barriers to care. The model honors the reality that healing is not a single intervention, but a pathway built over time through breath, movement, rest, relationship, and choice. description: Class begins with a thorough set of exercises at the barre that last from 30 to 45 minutes. Ballet originated in the Italian Renaissance courts around 1500 as large balls or spectacles that were performed by members of the royal court. The French king, Louis XIV, created the first academy and the positions, steps, and movements of the ballet were collected and codified. The spectacles began to be performed by artists that were trained in the academy, originally as part of an opera, and later as ballets that told a story through music, mime, and dance. Over the centuries ballet has influenced folk dance styles of many (mainly European) nations and, more recently, has been influenced by folk, modern, and contemporary forms of dance from all countries. title: Ayad Akhtar at The Brattle Theatre
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Ayad Akhtar —Pulitzer Prize–winning playwright, and acclaimed author of American Dervish and Homeland Elegies— for a discussion of his new novel, The Radiance . He will be joined in conversation by Indira Lakshmanan —co-host of NPR & WBUR’s Here & Now . Ayad Akhtar is a novelist and playwright. His work has been published and performed in over two dozen languages. He is the winner of the Pulitzer Prize for Drama, the Edith Wharton Citation of Merit for Fiction, and an award in literature from the American Academy of Arts and Letters, among other honors. Akhtar is the author of the novels American Dervish , a Kirkus Reviews Best Book of the Year, and Homeland Elegies , named one of 10 Best Books of 2020 by The New York Times . He has also authored the plays McNeal , Junk , Disgraced , The Who & The What , and The Invisible Hand. Akhtar was named the New York State Author in 2021. Photo Credit: Vincent Tullo Indira Lakshmanan is co-host of NPR & WBUR’s Here & Now . A veteran foreign correspondent and political reporter with decades of experience covering global events and U.S. policy, Lakshmanan has previously contributed to numerous NPR shows as a guest host and journalist, including 1A , On Point , Weekend Edition and Here & Now . Previously, she was the ideas and opinions editor at U.S. News & World Report and led the organization’s effort to showcase a wide range of perspectives. description: Classes will be broken into 5 sections at Level 1. New sessions start the first Monday of every odd month. No partner required. *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. *Students who purchase a membership for the Dance Complex will get that $25 taken off their 10 class new student rate, bringing it down to $85. Linear Salsa is a hybrid dance that comes from Mambo (a Cuban style that was popularized in the 1950’s NYC Palladium). NY Mambo is a marriage of footwork and partner-work from Cuba (Aftro-Cuban movements, Cuban Son) and the U.S. (Jazz, Swing). Salsa is a marketing term popularized in the 1970’s to commodify all Latin music and dance to a U.S. audience. Circular Salsa primarily comes from the Cuban dance Casino, which itself originates from Cuban Son. Salsa is by nature transformational, multinational, and multigenerational, embodying the shared heritage of Latin music. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I was the assistant teacher of this class for over 2 years under Ricardo Contreras. title: Live Blues & Roots Music Returns to Harvard Square: Wednesday Nights @ The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar
description: The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar and The Barrett Anderson Band are excited to announce a new weekly series, Blues & Roots Wednesdays , bringing live music back home to historic Harvard Square. “Cambridge, our fair city, and I share deep roots, and I’m thrilled to find a new musical home at The Sea Hag,” says Massachusetts-based singer/guitarist, Barrett Anderson. “Good music and good food are two of our most basic, fundamental needs,” he continues, “What great joy they give us. I am so happy to revel in that every Wednesday night with my dearest musical friends, and Kari and her incredible team at The Sea Hag. We go way back together, and I can’t imagine all the fun we have ahead.” Indeed, Anderson has strong connections to this scene. He remembers: “My first professional experience came when I was 15, backing up Muddy Waters’ band alums Pinetop Perkins and Bob Margolin at the original House of Blues on Winthrop Street. A few months after that I began busking, you’d often find me in Brattle Square or by the pit. This would have been mid/late 90s.” While still a teen, Anderson was a member of The Monster Mike Welch Band and Ronnie Earl & The Broadcasters (“Ronnie was my guitar hero. Then he was my teacher, then my boss. Now he’s my musical Father,” Anderson says), before eventually starting The Barrett Anderson Band in 2007. Anderson won a Boston Music Award (2013 Blues Artist of the Year), was on the Billboard charts (2020’s live album Hynoboogie spent 3 weeks on the Billboard Blues Album chart, peaking at #6), and was nominated for a Blues Music Award (2023 Band of the Year with Anthony Geraci & The Boston Blues All-Stars), all the while playing nationally, internationally, and locally in Cambridge and the greater Boston area. In addition to the musical roots, long-time locals may recognize Anderson from a decade serving tables and bartending at The Sea Hag’s sister establishment, Grendel’s Den, or from Abodeon, the mid-century modern shop started by his family. title: Bad Words Book Bash with Ríoghnach Robinson
description: Bad Words follows critic Selina Chan, whose blistering review turned Parker Navarro’s debut novel into the flop of the decade. Four years later, his new book offers a chance at redemption, but her second takedown sparks a viral literary feud. As the publishing world feasts on their public rivalry, a quieter dialogue begins—one that challenges their ideas about success, sincerity, and each other. Incisive and tender, Bad Words lays bare the costs of creation, the tension between ambition and integrity, the vulnerability of being seen, and the unexpected closeness between critique and care. In conversation with local Bookstagrammer Jess Lee, Ríoghnach will discuss writing romance born from rivalry, the culture of publishing and literary criticism, and the ways public narratives can shape private relationships. Following the author talk, stick around for a meet and greet with the author. Ríoghnach will sign and personalize Bad Words as well as up to two titles brought from home. 6:30 PM: Doors Open – Settle in to your seat and work on a Bad Words themed activity sheet while you wait for the discussion to begin! 7:00 PM: Discussion Begins – Ríoghnach and Jess will dive into Bad Words. 7:45 PM: Q&A Session – Your chance to ask the author anything! 8:00 PM: Signatures, Snapping Pics, and Salutations – Meet the author , get your book signed, snap a photo, and feel free to shop the store for your next favorite read! 8:30 PM : Head to the register to make any final purchases. 9:00 PM: Event Wraps Up – Thanks for joining us!

title: Cal Hoffman at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Cal Hoffman —acclaimed author of Easy to Slip— for a discussion of his new novel, Judah Can’t Tell. He will be joined in conversation by Joanna Rakoff —author of the international bestselling memoir My Salinger Year and the prize-winning novel A Fortunate Age. About Judah Can’t Tell On the morning a powerful US senator is accused of a long-buried sexual scandal, his son Harris wakes to a world suddenly unrecognizable. A journalist, husband, and father, Harris has built his life on reason, responsibility, and restraint. But as headlines spread and reputations unravel, he is pulled back into the unresolved gravity of his childhood—into memories of political ambition, parental absence, and a father whose public idealism shaped Harris’s private life in ways he is only beginning to understand. As Harris navigates a single charged day—balancing work, marriage, parenthood, and a culture hungry for judgment— Judah Can’t Tell becomes a powerful meditation on power, consent, masculinity, and moral inheritance. What do we owe the people we love when the truth threatens to destroy them? And what do we owe our children when silence feels safer than honesty? Written with emotional acuity and moral clarity, Judah Can’t Tell is a timely, deeply human novel about reckoning—personal, political, and generational.

title: Solo Aging Series (Virtual)

Take an honest look at your current support circle, identify gaps, and understand why the right people in the right roles matters more than we think. Session 2 (October 1): Practical Tools for Planning Ahead This session walks through what documents, decisions and systems to have in place, how to choose the right support and how to organize your financial and digital life so someone can step in if needed. Session 3 (October 15): Taking Action: Mindset, Legacy, and Making it Stick Here we'll address the emotional barriers that keep us stuck, reframing planning as something we do for ourselves and not a sign of decline. title: Victorian Science and the Beyond: Ethereal Evening Tours
description: The spirit-world around this world of sense Floats like an atmosphere, and everywhere Wafts through these earthly mists and vapours dense A vital breath of more ethereal air. -From “Haunted Houses” by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow Scientific discovery – and the promise of glimpsing the world beyond our perception – captured the imaginations of 19th century Americans. Join Longfellow House-Washington’s Headquarters for a special evening of historic house tours exploring the intersections of Victorian scientific thought, the lure of the supernatural, and their echoes today. 50-minute tours will invite participants to examine the unknown as we consider the Longfellow family’s entanglements with forensics and phrenology, early views of outer space, the spiritualism movement, and their pioneering use of ether anesthesia. Please note: This tour will include sensitive but frank discussions of 19th century violence, medical procedures, and drug use. Please use discretion when registering.

title: Sharon Weinberger at the Cambridge Public Library
description: RSVP is required for this event. Harvard Book Store and the Cambridge Public Library welcome Sharon Weinberger —veteran national security correspondent , and former National Security Editor at The Wall Street Journal from 2022 to 2026—for a discussion of her new book, Valley of Death: How Big Tech Is Fueling the Future of War . She will be joined in conversation by Sam Fellman —US Navy veteran with 17 years of journalism experience covering military affairs, currently studying disruptions in military technology and the civil-military order as a Knight Science Journalism fellow at MIT. Sharon Weinberger has been writing on national security issues for more than twenty-five years. She was the National Security Editor at The Wall Street Journal from 2022 to 2026 and has also contributed to The New York Times , New York Magazine , and The Washington Post, among other outlets . Also the author of The Imagineers of War: The Untold Story of DARPA, the Pentagon Agency that Changed the World , A Nuclear Family Vacation: Travels in the World of Atomic Weaponry , and Imaginary Weapons: A Journey Through the Pentagon’s Scientific Underworld , she is a member of the Council on Foreign Relations and has held fellowships at the Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University, MIT’s Knight Science Journalism program, and the Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars. She lives in Washington, DC. Photo Credit: Pete Kiehart Sam Fellman is a US Navy veteran with 17 years of journalism experience covering military affairs. He has worked for Harper’s Magazine, Military Times, and most recently led Business Insider’s defense team. Sam is currently studying disruptions in military technology and the civil-military order as a Knight Science Journalism fellow at MIT.

title: Victorian Science and the Beyond: Ethereal Evening Tours
description: The spirit-world around this world of sense Floats like an atmosphere, and everywhere Wafts through these earthly mists and vapours dense A vital breath of more ethereal air. -From “Haunted Houses” by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow Scientific discovery – and the promise of glimpsing the world beyond our perception – captured the imaginations of 19th century Americans. Join Longfellow House-Washington’s Headquarters for a special evening of historic house tours exploring the intersections of Victorian scientific thought, the lure of the supernatural, and their echoes today. 50-minute tours will invite participants to examine the unknown as we consider the Longfellow family’s entanglements with forensics and phrenology, early views of outer space, the spiritualism movement, and their pioneering use of ether anesthesia. Drawing from decades of study with master teachers and over thirty years of performance experience, Johara offers expert guidance in a supportive, inspiring environment—honoring the depth of this ancient art while inviting each student to discover their own unique style within it. Instructions: Wear comfortable dance or workout clothing that allows you to move freely. Classes are danced barefoot or in dance shoes. Students will be encouraged to acquire a veil and finger cymbals (zsagaat/ills). Cash preferred, or Venmo Drop-ins always welcome! What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? The more authentic name for this dance form is raqs sharqi (“dance of the East”), and its roots lie in the Middle and Near East, primarily in Egypt and Turkey. This dance form was introduced to the United States and Europe at the turn of the 20th century, but it was not widely performed or taught until the 1950s and 1960s, when the belly dance craze swept across the U.S. The American cabaret style of belly dance is rooted in the legacy passed down by notable American teachers and performers, who blended Middle Eastern influences with their own innovations and movement styles drawn from diverse dance backgrounds. description: This class starts with understanding salsa music’s rhythm and timing in addition to a brief history of the music and dance. You will learn the basic steps and partnering fundamentals. It later developed in New York and it’s popular throughout Latin America in places like Puerto Rico, Colombia, Peru and Cuba just to name a few. title: Ellen Warner at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Ellen Warner —author of The Second Half: Forty Women Reveal Life After Fifty— for a discussion of her new book, The Other Half: Forty Men Reveal Life After Fifty. About The Other Half An insightful and intimate look at aging and masculinity that includes interviews and portraits of men from around the world. What do men really think? From a taxi driver to a prince, a fishmonger to a professional boxer, The Other Half reveals the inner thoughts of men over fifty from different nationalities and different walks of life in their own words, illuminated by their portraits. Author and photojournalist Ellen Warner traveled the world to find out what men really think about love, work, and aging, speaking with well-known figures like film director James Ivory and journalist Bill Keller, as well as a philosopher, a chess grandmaster, a hair stylist, a financier, and more. Interviewing men from Colombia, Greece, Saudi Arabia, Sierra Leone, Sweden, and everywhere in between, Warner assembles a moving portrait of their reflections, insights, challenges, and hard-won triumphs. A companion to The Second Half: Forty Women Reveal Life After Fifty , Warner’s latest book shares the diverse, vibrant experiences of men over fifty.

title: MAIN STAGE: Wayman Chin | Sweet Land | Faculty Artist Recital
description: “Sweet land, we sing to thee….” Mirrored reflections on the mystic chords of memory As we look back on the 250 years since the founding of our nation, we hold a mirror of hopes cast and yet to be realized, all generated by a spirit of intensity, invention, and re-invention. To mark our nation’s semiquincentennial, faculty pianist and Dean Emeritus Wayman Chin presents a program of pieces that reflect the American psyche, including works by Aaron Copland, Samuel Barber and Leonard Bernstein; Beethoven’s Seven Variations on “God Save the King,” (to whose melody Samuel Francis Smith penned new lyrics we know as “My Country, ’tis of thee”) and contemporary composers Jeremy Van Buskirk and Nico Muhly, whose “Refine” for solo piano is a short variation on “America the Beautiful.” Longy’s performance are free and open to the public, but please register in advance.

title: Oktoberfest: Choucroute & American Wines – Wine Tasting Class
description: What should you drink with choucroute when the wines are American? Join internationally renowned sommelier Bertil Jean-Chronberg for a lively 90-minute wine-and-food experience inspired by the convivial spirit of a German wine hall. Explore how different styles of American wine interact with the richness of sausages and pork, the acidity of sauerkraut, mustard, spices and all the savory complexity of this classic dish. Taste several contrasting American wines alongside choucroute and discover why acidity, sweetness, aromatic intensity and texture can completely change a pairing. More importantly, learn how to recognize what works, and why. So, you can apply the same principles to your own table. As always at Bonde, expect serious wine without the seriousness: only 16 participants, generous conversation, plenty of tasting, food and wine, and a relaxed, unpretentious atmosphere where there are no wrong questions. title: Level 2B Salsa
description: This class reviews cross-body lead and covers inside turn, half right turn, and cumbia turns, combining them with basic right and left turns. Partnering technique is emphasized focusing on proper hand/arm hold and placement. Freestyle footwork and musicality is also introduced. Cost: $20 Single Class | $90 for 5-Class Package *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. REGISTER HERE Accepted Payments: Cash, Check, Venmo (@salsaycontroldance), PayPal, CashApp ($JohnnyGiraldo80), Zelle What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Salsa is a musical and dance style that originated in Cuba with African roots and European influences. It later developed in New York and it’s popular throughout Latin America in places like Puerto Rico, Colombia, Peru and Cuba just to name a few. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I grew up listening to Salsa music and later got interested in the dance. As a teenager, I was part of a Colombian folk dance group before starting to perform Salsa duets with my brother Andres. I’ve been teaching Salsa for about 27 years now and this year we are celebrating 23 years of our dance company, Salsa y Control. Finish this statement: I am passionate about teaching this style because… It allows people to connect in a unique way. Salsa dancing is a social dance that help break barriers and brings people together from all walks of life. It also gives you the opportunity to express yourself freely on the dance floor or stage. How can students learn more about this offering? description: The All Levels House class expands on foundations learned in the Intro class. Dance experience is a plus, but is not required. Students will dive deeper into developing their basic vocabulary, musical understanding and will learn how to connect concepts through choreography AND improvisation. Class is physical but fun! Come to class with an open mind and a comfortable pair of shoes. Cost: $20 Single Class | $95 for 5-Class Card | $185 for 10-Class Card (class cards may be used toward all Dance Complex house classes) *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. REGISTER HERE Accepted Payments: Cash, Venmo (@sean-bjerke), Paypal/Zelle (beejerks@gmail.com), Credit Card through Pre-registration What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? One of the world’s most popular music genres, “house” is an electronic dance music genre that emerged in Chicago in the late 70s/early 80s following the disco era. The term “house” was derived from The Warehouse, a Chicago club where the music was often played. Though the essence of the dance is purely freestyle, popular steps performed in NYC dance clubs were eventually recognized as “house dance foundation.” Members of NYC’s Dance Fusion were the first to teach house dance, which contributed greatly to house becoming a worldwide phenomenon. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? A master Taekwondo-ist and professional dancer, Sean began dancing in the year 2000, and was formally introduced to house dance by Boston native Ricardo Foster Jr in 2007. For years, Sean sought opportunities to learn from and train under many house dance teachers including Jardy Santiago, members of NYC’s Dance Fusion, and Edson Gonzaga who helped unlock Sean’s understanding of house music and develop his own personal dance style. Since 2013 Sean has been an active member of Boston’s underground club scene aft

description: Students can expect a welcoming and engaging class that brings together Capoeira’s movement, music, rhythm, self-defense, and cultural traditions. Capoeira is an Afro-Brazilian art form developed in Brazil by enslaved Africans and their descendants, bringing together elements of martial arts, movement, music, and cultural expression. We teach Capoeira Contemporânea, which draws from the traditions of both Capoeira Regional and Capoeira Angola while incorporating influences that have developed throughout Brazil. With over 50 years of continuous Capoeira practice and more than 40 years of teaching experience, I founded Associação de Capoeira Mandingueiros dos Palmares (Capoeira MdP) in 1977 in Belo Horizonte, Brazil. Our practice of Capoeira Contemporânea is deeply rooted in the traditions of Capoeira Regional developed by Mestre Bimba. title: Flamenco: Fiesta por bulerías with Nino de los Reyes
description: The evening begins with a joyful and engaging Flamenco class open to all levels, from complete beginners to experienced dancers. We will work with the codes and language of Bulerías, discovering its rhythm, energy, and spirit in a welcoming and playful environment. After the lesson, we will explore Bulerías through its most expressive and spontaneous side, the way Flamenco artists come together to share, connect, and celebrate through music and movement in community. Everyone is welcome – come join the fiesta! NINO DE LOS REYES: Nino begins his career at 9 years old with the “Campanas Flamencas” show, directed by Paco Sanchez, founder of the renowned company “Cumbre Flamenca”, sharing stage with: Joaquin Grilo, Milagros Mengibar, La Tati, Antonio Reyes and his brother Isaac de los Reyes. At the same age, he starts joining greater dance companies like Eduardo Serrano “El Guito”, Carmen Cortes and Javier Baron among others. He was invited to join the “Beyond the Memory” show, a tribute to Paco de Lucia, where he had the opportunity to share the scenario with the renowned members of his band. Also, he was a guest in the mediaset show, “Flamencos en el Berlin”, collaborating with the greatest representatives of flamenco dance to date: Antonio Canales, Juan Manuel Fernández Montoya “Farruquito”, Antonio Fernández Montoya “Farru”, José Maya, Paloma Fantova and Belen Lopez. Currently, due to his versatility, dancing and musical knowledge has collaborated with various recordings related to pop and jazz genres. Just to mention some, “Stranger to Stranger” album from worldwide Singer Paul Simon, with whom he performed in the “Barclays center” in Madrid, in front of 20,000 people. In addition, Chick Corea, jazz’s legendary figure, invited him to participate in his 75th birthday presentation in the Blue Note club and performing in the Madison Square Garden in New York. title: Liza Black at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store and the Carr-Ryan Center for Human Rights welcome Liza Black —associate professor of history and of Native American and Indigenous studies at Indiana University and author of Picturing Indians: Native Americans in Film, 1941–1960 —for a discussion of her new book, How Settlers Get Away with Murder: The Killing of Indigenous Women and Two-Spirit People in the Americas. About How Settlers Get Away With Murder A forensic history of the missing and murdered Indigenous women and Two-Spirit people crisis that unmasks the Americas’ oldest and most relentless crime: Native genocide. Since the arrival of Columbus, thousands of perpetrators have gotten away with murder, burying evidence of their crimes in police reports and court testimony. How Settlers Get Away with Murder unearths that hidden evidence to expose the ongoing crisis of missing and murdered Indigenous women and Two-Spirit people (MMIW2S). Historian and citizen of Cherokee Nation Liza Black examines 5 cases in Canada, the US, and Mexico, from 1908 to 2017. Rejecting narratives that blame victims’ poverty or trauma, Black dissects police files, coroners’ reports, and court records to uncover a harsh historical reality: The evidence of settler violence has been hiding in plain sight. This landmark work delivers a damning verdict: The same systems of law and policing that have targeted Native people for centuries have also shielded their killers. Through meticulous archival interrogation, Black demonstrates how police, courts, and coroners have functioned not as instruments of justice but as pillars of a system designed to protect settler violence.

title: Listen To This: Celebrating 100 Years of Miles Davis
description: One of the pivotal moments in our music lifetimes came when Miles Davis traded in his tailored Italian suits for mod psychedelic threads, and re-engineered his music with grooves from Sly Stone and James Brown and guitars from Jimi Hendrix. Created with a parade of genius collaborators, In a Silent Way, Bitches Brew, Jack Johnson, Live/Evil, On the Corner and other albums wrote new playbooks for jazz improvisers. Out of that matrix emerged multiple lineages, but nobody ever did it quite like Miles and company. The eight members of Listen to This revive, refresh and inhabit this music fearlessly. Led by Morphine’s founding drummer Jerome Deupree, LTT features Ornette Coleman keyboardist Dave Bryant, Either/Orchestra leader Russ Gershon on woodwinds and organ, Bim Skala Bim percussionist Rick Barry, trumpeter Bryan Murphy, bassist Rick McLaughlin, guitarist J. Johnson, and Todd Brunel in the essential and mysterious bass clarinet role.

title: Spotlight Tour: Coloring the Past, with Jide Anekwe ’28
description: Know Before You Go How to join: Check in at the Visitor Services desk; space is limited. Fee: This is a free event. Accessibility accommodations: If you would like to request accommodations for your visit, please contact Visitor Services at am_register@harvard.edu or 617-495-9400. For more details about accommodations at the museums, please see the Accessibility page. General info: The museum visit page has general guidelines for your visit. On this tour, Jide Anekwe ‘28 will look at the significance of color in the ancient Mediterranean world and at modern perceptions of the past. The stops on the tour are: Portrait of a woman, a painting from Roman Imperial Egypt (c. 130–150 CE); Youthful hero or god, a marble sculpture from Imperial Rome (1st–2nd century CE) after a Greek sculpture by Skopas from the fourth century BCE; and William Holman Hunt’s painting The Miracle of the Sacred Fire, Church of the Holy Sepulchre (1892–99). Spotlight Tours are designed and led by Harvard undergraduates from a range of academic disciplines. Each tour is focused on objects chosen by the student and provides visitors a unique, thematic view into the collections. Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. Open to the public, these tours start outside the museum shop on Saturdays and Sundays at 11am and 2pm. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. The Ho Family Student Guide Program at the Harvard Art Museums prepares students to develop original, research-based tours. Through their training, Student Guides gain knowledge of the collections and develop skills in critical thinking, visual analysis, public speaking, and leadership. Find out what the Student Guides are up to anytime on Instagram @harvardarthappens.

title: Nature and Mount Auburn
description: Join us for a mindful walk through the landscape, exploring the history and founding of Mount Auburn Cemetery. From its beginning, Mount Auburn Cemetery has drawn on nature as a resource for comfort, a focus of study, and a guide for developing its sacred landscape. Its founding, in 1831, influenced the expansion of garden cemeteries, the future development of landscape architecture, and the national park movement. This tour will include visits to the Asa Gray Garden, Consecration Dell, and the monuments of Jacob Bigelow, Margaret Fuller, and Henry Wadsworth Longfellow. Expect to enhance your understanding of the cemetery’s rich history, and learn how the study of botany, transcendentalism, and environmental neuroscience has helped us to understand the ways that nature sustains and inspires us. Tour Guide: Barry J. Kahn Barry J. Kahn is one of twenty volunteer docents who staff the Welcome Center at Mount Auburn Cemetery. When he retired as a social worker in July 2025, Barry began to create a tour centered on illuminating how places, like Mount Auburn Cemetery, promote peace of mind. Comfortable walking shoes recommended. Check-in at Welcome Center

title: Spotlight Tour: Thresholds, with Jane Lilly ’27
description: On this tour, Jane Lilly ’27 will discuss boundaries and in-betweenness, exploring how we see and move through works of art. The stops on the tour include a lintel (Fez, Morocco, Marinid period, early to mid-14th century); a stained glass window, titled Scene from the Life of Thomas Becket (Canterbury, England, c. 1190–1205); and the painting Piazza San Marco, Venice (c. 1730–34) by Canaletto. Spotlight Tours are designed and led by Harvard undergraduates from a range of academic disciplines. Each tour is focused on objects chosen by the student and provides visitors a unique, thematic view into the collections. Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. Open to the public, these tours start outside the museum shop on Saturdays and Sundays at 11am and 2pm. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. The Ho Family Student Guide Program at the Harvard Art Museums prepares students to develop original, research-based tours. Through their training, Student Guides gain knowledge of the collections and develop skills in critical thinking, visual analysis, public speaking, and leadership. Find out what the Student Guides are up to anytime on Instagram @harvardarthappens.

title: Walking Tour: Constructing Nature in Harvard Yard
description: Join us for a special gallery talk that includes a walking tour! Graduate student teacher Ryan Schmidt-Knapik will first discuss the exhibition On Location: Drawing the Outdoors in the galleries before leading a walking tour on campus, where you will learn how to interpret and appreciate nature in our urban landscape. We will focus on exploring how plant form, function, and the history of non-native species introduction have shaped the biology of human-dominated landscapes. Led by: Ryan Schmidt-Knapik, Graduate student teacher and Ph.D. candidate in the Department of Organismic and Evolutionary Biology, Harvard University On Location: Drawing the Outdoors features drawings by J. M. W. Turner, John Constable, Gustave Courbet, Edouard Manet, Berthe Morisot, Paul Cézanne, and Vincent van Gogh, among many others. The exhibition is on view from September 18, 2026 to January 17, 2027. Funding for the exhibition and related programming was provided by the Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Support Fund, the Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Support Fund for the Study of Dutch Drawing, the Melvin R. Seiden and Janine Luke Fund for Publications and Exhibitions, and the M. Victor Leventritt Lecture Series Endowment Fund. The catalogue was made possible by the Andrew W. Mellon Publication Funds. Additional project support was provided by the Almathea Charitable Foundation.

title: “Worthy to be Any Man’s Friend”: Lecture on Henry David Thoreau
description: Join historian Richard Smith for a lecture in Story Chapel on Henry David Thoreau and notable figures in Mount Auburn. Henry David Thoreau was one of the most important and influential writers of the 19th Century. And while he isn’t buried in Mount Auburn Cemetery, he was well acquainted with many of the literary and political figures who are. Join Concord historian Richard Smith for a presentation about Henry Thoreau and some of his famous friends. The “Hermit of Walden Pond” wasn’t such a hermit after all. Longfellow, Charles Sumner and Margaret Fuller are just some of the notable figures who are buried here that Thoreau knew and associated with. And he even liked some of them! Following the lecture, Richard will lead a walk to see some of the graves of notable figures.

title: Spotlight Tour: Un/Settled, with Leandra Bautista ’28
description: On this tour, Leandra Bautista ’28 will look closely at three works of art that evoke home as a space of either comfort or discomfort. The stops on the tour are Woman on a Striped Sofa with a Dog (1876) by Mary Cassatt; a 12th-century Italian casket in the shape of a tower; and Robert Smullyan Sloan’s 1945 painting of a Black soldier. Spotlight Tours are designed and led by Harvard undergraduates from a range of academic disciplines. Each tour is focused on objects chosen by the student and provides visitors a unique, thematic view into the collections. Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. Open to the public, these tours start outside the museum shop on Saturdays and Sundays at 11am and 2pm. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. The Ho Family Student Guide Program at the Harvard Art Museums prepares students to develop original, research-based tours. Through their training, Student Guides gain knowledge of the collections and develop skills in critical thinking, visual analysis, public speaking, and leadership. Find out what the Student Guides are up to anytime on Instagram @harvardarthappens.

title: MAIN STAGE: Dana Maiben and Vivian Montgomery | An Outburst of Improvisors | Faculty Artist Recital
description: An Outburst of Improvisors: 17th Century Music for Violin and Harpsichord In 1600s Italy, the performer and the composer were the same person, and nobody was playing it safe. Opera was being invented. The madrigal was being torn apart and rebuilt. Women were writing and publishing everywhere: on the opera stage, in their own salons, inside cloistered convents. Musicians improvised their way into an entirely new style of virtuoso songwriting, and four hundred years later it still sounds reckless. This intimate program for violin and harpsichord covers the whole range: instrumental covers of the pop songs of the day, some of the earliest violin sonatas ever written, ground-bass mash-ups, and plenty of improvising in the moment. Music by Barbara Strozzi, Biagio Marini, Chiara Margarita Cozzolani, Claudio Monteverdi, Dario Castello, Girolamo Frescobaldi, Isabella Leonarda, Marco Uccellini, Michelangelo Rossi, and Salamone Rossi, plus the premiere of a new improvisation-based work by John Morrison. Longy’s performance are free and open to the public, but please register in advance.

Majestic Healing Pathways™ is the foundational care model that guides all of Majestic Community Wellness’s programs. It reflects our belief that healing is a right — not a privilege — and that healing happens most sustainably when care is consistent, culturally grounded, and rooted in community. Developed in response to gaps in traditional health and wellness systems, Majestic Healing Pathways™ centers the lived experiences of Black and Brown communities who face disproportionate stress, trauma, and barriers to care. The model honors the reality that healing is not a single intervention, but a pathway built over time through breath, movement, rest, relationship, and choice. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? For more than 20 years, Nora has been teaching yoga and dance to students of all ages. She completed her 200-hour teacher training at Atmananda Yoga, and her teaching continues to be informed by years of study in Pilates, Feldenkrais, Hot Yoga, and Katonah Yoga. The births of her two children inspired her to deepen her studies in prenatal and postnatal yoga. She focused much of her teaching on supporting families and children through the various stages of development. The School of Classical Ballet was founded in 1985 by Anna Myer and Patricia Adelmann. For over 30 years, the school has provided students with classical ballet training and helped to develop student appreciation for dance as an art form. The School of Classical Ballet is a technique-based school with emphasis on learning. Performances are all-inclusive for students to showcase their technique and gain experience performing for an audience. title: Julie Orringer at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Julie Orringer —author of three award-winning books: How to Breathe Underwater , The Invisible Bridge , and T he Flight Portfolio , which was the basis for the 2023 Netflix series Transatlantic —for a discussion of her new novel, Luna, Phoenix, Queen . She will be joined in conversation by Jayne Anne Phillips —author of the Pulitzer Prize-winning novel Night Watch . About Luna, Phoenix, Queen A spellbinding tour de force from the bestselling author of The Invisible Bridge —a novel about varieties of infidelity, the provenance of a literary masterpiece, and the power of storytelling to shape identity and destiny. Dava and Barr Pennington, professors at a Midwestern university, both harbor potent secrets. Fiction writing is his specialty; English literature is hers. But Dava is unhappy in their marriage, and secretly in love with a colleague, Svetlana White, who teaches in the Russian Studies department; spurred by their complicated liaison, she spends her nights working on a novel about two women who run a domestic violence shelter in coastal Maine. Though she loves the work and the refuge it provides, the writing becomes increasingly difficult as her memory begins to fail; tests reveal that she’s suffering from early-onset Alzheimer’s. After a precipitous decline, she moves to a memory-care facility in a neighboring town. Soon afterward, her husband, alone in the house at night, discovers her hidden manuscript, which he reads with envy, and then with anger, as he extrapolates his wife’s affair from the relationship described in the novel’s pages. Over the next two years he rewrites the novel and publishes it as his own, to wide acclaim. But persistent feelings of guilt lead him to confess his theft to an unlikely party, who leads others to the truth. Luna, Phoenix, Queen tells its tale of artistic and marital betrayal in a chorus of voices. We hear from Barr as he becomes obsessed with Luna, a horrifically injured dog at a local shelter;

What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I am a dance artist, teacher and performer as well as a clinical social worker. title: Art + Science: Papermaking
description: Have you ever wondered what happens in our conservation labs? In this session, Penley Knipe, the Philip and Lynn Straus Senior Conservator of Works on Paper and head of the Paper Lab, will talk about the history of paper, including how it is made and what it can tell us about a work of art. The Straus Center for Conservation and Technical Studies is a world leader in fine arts conservation, research, and training. title: The Gilded Rose Book Bash with Joanna Shupe & Sarah MacLean
description: Join USA Today bestselling author Joanna Shupe for The Gilded Rose Book Bash, a celebration of an angst-filled, Beauty and the Beast inspired romance set amid the excess and opulence of Gilded Age New York. Caroline thought she was stepping into a fairy tale when she married Manhattan’s most sought-after bachelor, but behind closed doors, her marriage becomes a nightmare. When the chance to catalogue a private library gives her a lifeline, Caroline finds not only the literary treasures she’s been missing, but also Zane Bishop, a brilliant, wealthy recluse who understands her pain and is determined to help set her free. Come hear Shupe in conversation with bestselling author and romance champion Sarah MacLean as they talk about resilience, forbidden passion, complicated heroines, and the transformative power of love. Following the conversation, stick around for a meet and greet with the author! Joanna will add personalizations to your pre-signed copies of The Gilded Rose as well as up to two of her titles brought from home. 6:30 PM: Doors Open – Grab your pre-signed book and a drink from the Lovestruck Bar & Cafe, settle in, and get ready for a great discussion! 7:00 PM: Discussion Begins – Joanna and Sarah will dive into The Gilded Rose. 7:45 PM: Q&A Session – Your chance to ask the author about their writing process! 8:00 PM: Signatures, Snapping Pics, and Salutations – Meet the author , and get your book personalized. 8:30 PM : Last call – Grab your final pour from the wine bar and head to the register for any book purchases. 9:00 PM: Event Wraps Up – Thanks for joining us!

description: Attend one of our most beloved, longest standing brewery traditions: Trivia Tuesday! Every Tuesday swing by our Broadway taproom for our weekly trivia night. It’s free to compete, and winners get beer money. Here’s how it works: show up with your team of 2 – 6 players starting at 7:00 pm, when we’ll open the doors to the back taproom. Head down the hallway to the back, then snag a seat. All seating is first come first serve, so we recommend arriving early – there generally is a line! Questions rotate every week, and cover categories ranging from history, politics, sports, movies, pop culture, music, and more. At the end of the game, 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place teams will be awarded Lamplighter gift cards – good for usage in either of our taprooms and at Pepita Coffee Co. In addition to Trivia Tuesday at our Broadway taproom, we also host weekly trivia at our CX taproom. That game takes place on Monday evenings, and is also free to join for teams of 2 – 6. We’d love to see you at either or both! Hungry? Munch on our signature giant soft pretzels or some crunchy nachos, which are available Tuesday evenings only. You’re also always welcome to bring your own food or order in, ask our staff for their favorite local recommendations. See you at trivia night! You must be 21+ attend, all guests will be asked to show valid government ID. Questions? Get in touch! You can reach us at events@lamplighterbrewing.com

title: Dr. Dariush Mozaffarian at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Dr. Dariush Mozaffarian —cardiologist, public health scientist, and Director of the Food is Medicine Institute at Tufts University—for a discussion of his debut book, Food Is Medicine: Healing Our Bodies, Nourishing Our Minds, and Transforming Our Food System. About Food Is Medicine An urgent exposé of how the food we eat is making us sick, how we can heal, and the revolutionary new food system that can mend our health, economy, and planet from a world-renowned expert on nutrition and public health. The food we eat is making us sick. In the nation and around the world, diet is now the leading cause of illness and premature death, from heart disease to the global pandemic of diabetes. Advocates of “healthy diets” pin the blame on overeating, but the bigger issue is that we undereat —we don’t consume enough nutritious food, food that nourishes and heals. Harnessing the power of the right foods can do more than prevent illness; it can treat it, extending life while reducing the crippling cost of ill health to our communities and economy. Food Is Medicine shows the way, from transforming our diets to keep us healthy to getting the right foods into our stores and onto our plates—all while eating plentifully and pleasurably. A global authority at the intersection of nutrition, medicine, and public policy, Dariush Mozaffarian, MD, DrPH draws on cutting-edge research to turn complex science into a clear, actionable program to end our health crisis. Exposing a broken food system, plagued by the harms of ultraprocessing and ruinous to the environment, he lays out exactly how the meals we eat are damaging our bodies. He reveals the medicinal, healing power of ideal nutrition and introduces the innovators who are pioneering solutions—at the doctor’s office, in supermarkets, in the halls of Congress, and above all for individuals, to empower them to access the foods they need to live well. title: Postpartum Movement with Nora Stephens
description: Postpartum Movement is a welcoming, supportive space to move, reconnect, and care for yourself during the postpartum journey. Through accessible movement, we’ll build strength and mobility, release tension, and support connection with your changing body. Move at your own pace, take breaks whenever you need, and choose what feels right for you. Babies are warmly welcome, but you do not need to bring your baby to participate. No previous movement or yoga experience is needed. All bodies, all levels, and all postpartum experiences are welcome. Come as you are. Cost: $0 – $22 Sliding Scale REGISTER HERE What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Majestic Healing Pathways™ is the foundational care model that guides all of Majestic Community Wellness’s programs. It reflects our belief that healing is a right — not a privilege — and that healing happens most sustainably when care is consistent, culturally grounded, and rooted in community. Developed in response to gaps in traditional health and wellness systems, Majestic Healing Pathways™ centers the lived experiences of Black and Brown communities who face disproportionate stress, trauma, and barriers to care. The model honors the reality that healing is not a single intervention, but a pathway built over time through breath, movement, rest, relationship, and choice. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? For more than 20 years, Nora has been teaching yoga and dance to students of all ages. She completed her 200-hour teacher training at Atmananda Yoga, and her teaching continues to be informed by years of study in Pilates, Feldenkrais, Hot Yoga, and Katonah Yoga. The births of her two children inspired her to deepen her studies in prenatal and postnatal yoga. She focused much of her teaching on supporting families and children through the various stages of development. During this time, she earned her Prenatal Yoga Certification through OM Yoga

description: Class begins with a thorough set of exercises at the barre that last from 30 to 45 minutes. Centre practice follows, and may consist of a battement tendu exercise, a battement jeté exercise, a grand battement exercise, small and/or large adage, stationary turns, traveling turns, and petite and grand allegro enchaînement (small and big jumps). Ballet originated in the Italian Renaissance courts around 1500 as large balls or spectacles that were performed by members of the royal court. The French king, Louis XIV, created the first academy and the positions, steps, and movements of the ballet were collected and codified. The spectacles began to be performed by artists that were trained in the academy, originally as part of an opera, and later as ballets that told a story through music, mime, and dance. Over the centuries ballet has influenced folk dance styles of many (mainly European) nations and, more recently, has been influenced by folk, modern, and contemporary forms of dance from all countries. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I had a professional dance career that spanned more than twenty years and included company work in both ballet and contemporary companies as well as dancing, choreographing, and teaching as a freelance artist.

title: Screening of Presence
description: Join us for a midday screening exploring how public life has been staged, recorded, and remembered on screen. Presence is a film installation by Jingrong Zhang, supported by the Council for the Arts at MIT (CAMIT). Drawing on archival and cinematic footage across cultures and historical periods, the work assembles a "global supercut" of public gatherings: moments of solitude, chance encounters, street life, and collective assembly. As the montage builds from isolated figures to dense crowds, it invites viewers to consider how strangers come together in public space, and how those moments of shared presence have been captured on screen across a century of image-making. Every crowd on screen was once as present as we are now.

title: The Many Lives of Theban Tomb 16
description: The ancient Egyptian tomb known as Theban Tomb 16 dates to the reign of Ramesses II in the 19th Dynasty of the New Kingdom (around 1250 BCE). Originally, it served as the burial place of a priest named Panehsy and his wife, Tarenu, a chantress. Long after their lifetimes, the tomb remained an important resting place and was reused for more than a thousand years by members of the Theban elite. By the late 19th or early 20th century, the tomb had been looted, and it suffered further plundering in the 1970s. Since 2008, however, a team from the University of Memphis has been working to document and conserve both the tomb and its many secondary burials. In this program, Egyptologist Suzanne Onstine will present the latest research on the tomb’s beautifully painted plaster scenes, exploring what they reveal about life in ancient Egypt as well as funerary culture during the first millennium BCE. Free event parking is available with registration. Register by October 20 to receive parking registration instructions. Advance registration is recommended. Presented by the Harvard Museum of the Ancient Near East in association with the Harvard Museums of Science & Culture. About the Speaker: Suzanne Onstine is an associate professor in the Department of History at the University of Memphis. She received her BA in Anthropology at the University of Arizona and her MA and PhD in Near and Middle Eastern Civilizations at the University of Toronto. She has conducted archaeological research in Egypt for thirty years and currently directs the University of Memphis mission to Theban Tomb 16 (TT16), the tomb of Panehsy in Dra Abu el-Naga, Luxor. She has published many works on women and religion in addition to various aspects of her research in TT16.

title: Beginner NY Salsa
description: Classes will be broken into 5 sections at Level 1. New sessions start the first Monday of every odd month. Warmup Footwork Review Foundational move for Level 1 On2 Linear Salsa (of which there are 7) Dance with Music Philosophically things to be on the lookout for, the importance of melding footwork and partner-work when dancing Salsa, the importance of spaced repetition, the importance of tying everything to Social dancing, and personal convolutional schemes to try to attenuate the lead/follow dichotomy. No partner required. *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. *Students who purchase a membership for the Dance Complex will get that $25 taken off their 10 class new student rate, bringing it down to $85. Cost: $23 Single Class | $85 for 5-Class Package | $130 for 10-Class Package | $110 for new student 10-class package Cash, Venmo (@Brendan-Folan), Zelle (bjfoley21@gmail.com) REGISTRATION: Not Required, Drop-Ins Welcome What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Linear Salsa is a hybrid dance that comes from Mambo (a Cuban style that was popularized in the 1950’s NYC Palladium). NY Mambo is a marriage of footwork and partner-work from Cuba (Aftro-Cuban movements, Cuban Son) and the U.S. (Jazz, Swing). Salsa is a marketing term popularized in the 1970’s to commodify all Latin music and dance to a U.S. audience. Circular Salsa primarily comes from the Cuban dance Casino, which itself originates from Cuban Son. Salsa is by nature transformational, multinational, and multigenerational, embodying the shared heritage of Latin music. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I was the assistant teacher of this class for over 2 years under Ricardo Contreras. title: Live Blues & Roots Music Returns to Harvard Square: Wednesday Nights @ The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar
description: The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar and The Barrett Anderson Band are excited to announce a new weekly series, Blues & Roots Wednesdays , bringing live music back home to historic Harvard Square. “Cambridge, our fair city, and I share deep roots, and I’m thrilled to find a new musical home at The Sea Hag,” says Massachusetts-based singer/guitarist, Barrett Anderson. “Good music and good food are two of our most basic, fundamental needs,” he continues, “What great joy they give us. I am so happy to revel in that every Wednesday night with my dearest musical friends, and Kari and her incredible team at The Sea Hag. We go way back together, and I can’t imagine all the fun we have ahead.” Indeed, Anderson has strong connections to this scene. He remembers: “My first professional experience came when I was 15, backing up Muddy Waters’ band alums Pinetop Perkins and Bob Margolin at the original House of Blues on Winthrop Street. A few months after that I began busking, you’d often find me in Brattle Square or by the pit. This would have been mid/late 90s.” While still a teen, Anderson was a member of The Monster Mike Welch Band and Ronnie Earl & The Broadcasters (“Ronnie was my guitar hero. Then he was my teacher, then my boss. Now he’s my musical Father,” Anderson says), before eventually starting The Barrett Anderson Band in 2007. Anderson won a Boston Music Award (2013 Blues Artist of the Year), was on the Billboard charts (2020’s live album Hynoboogie spent 3 weeks on the Billboard Blues Album chart, peaking at #6), and was nominated for a Blues Music Award (2023 Band of the Year with Anthony Geraci & The Boston Blues All-Stars), all the while playing nationally, internationally, and locally in Cambridge and the greater Boston area. In addition to the musical roots, long-time locals may recognize Anderson from a decade serving tables and bartending at The Sea Hag’s sister establishment, Grendel’s Den, or from Abodeon, the mid-century modern shop started by his family. title: Kenzō Tange Lecture: Maria Claudia Clemente and Francesco Isidori “The Architecture of Public Space”
description: Today, approximately 56% of the world’s population—equivalent to 4.7 billion people—live in urban areas, and that number is constantly growing. This phenomenon of unchecked growth, evident in both global megacities and “old” European cities, has led to the pulverization of the very concept of the city. In this context, the public space around which Europe’s great cities were built—the space of thecivitas, major collective events and street demonstrations, as well as, more simply, the place where one encounters the “other”—seems to be vanishing, giving way to a void of quality and identity. To bring public space back to the center of the debate, we must reflect on a different vision of the city, one structured around the form of public space, that architecture can help shape and enrich. Drawing on the reflections inThe Architecture of Public Space(Park Books, 2023), the lecture will illustrate several examples from Labics’s recent architectural work, where the connection between architecture, the city, and public space is most evident.
