description: The TUNEabomber SHOW DESCRIPTION: Set at a parole board hearing, Ted Kaczynski (aka The Unabomber) recounts his life through song in the hope of proving that he never wanted to be a monster, he only wanted to be a star. While he may have spent years sending explosives, this is one performance Ted can’t bomb. Written and performed by John Lampe and Michael Wysong, this new musical comedy dares to ask the question no one needed an answer to: What if this notorious eco-terrorist was the next Bob Fosse? ARTIST SOCIAL MEDIA: @thetuneabomber ARTIST BIOS: Michael Wysong is a Manhattan-based musical theatre composer and lyricist who was described by Cabaret Scenes as “a wry and clever songwriter and political satirist in the tradition of Tom Lehrer…a major talent to be kept track of.” His work has been performed at cabaret venues and theatres throughout New York City, including the Triad Theatre and Feinstein’s/54 Below. Recent credits include new music for a production of Marat/Sade, music and sound design for Macbeth (New York Shakespeare Company), and music and sound design for Aunt Jack (Theater for the New City). He also wrote the book and lyrics for a new adaptation of The Revenger’s Tragedy, music and lyrics for the song cycle Love is…, and contributed a song to CHANGEMAKERS with Tony Nominated lyricist Bill Russell for their shared alma mater, The University of Kansas. John Lampe is a director, writer, and performer. His work has been seen across the US and in Europe. In New York, he has worked with companies such as Urban Stages, New Circle Theatre, Frog and Peach Theatre, and ANDTheatre, where he served as Artistic Director. His two man musical comedy “The TUNEabomber” plays monthly in New York at The Reverie Room. Keep in touch at www.johnlampe.com . title: Jaqueline Tyrwhitt Urban Design Lecture: Dana Cuff “Coming Home: Crisis, Fire, and Recovery”
description: Dr. Dana Cuff, an educator, scholar, designer, and activist who explores how design can contribute to building more just and equitable cities, work on rebuilding after the 2025 Eaton Fire in Altadena and the housing crisis in Los Angeles. In 2006, Cuff founded cityLAB, a research and design center that initiates experimental projects to explore more equitable metropolitan possibilities. Starting in 2019, cityLAB expanded its social and political engagement by creating long term partnerships with community organizations in the region, first in the Westlake/MacArthur Park neighborhood of Los Angeles, and after the devastating fires of 2025, in Altadena. cityLAB has developed sustainable, high-performance, low-cost housing prototypes for infill sites ranging from backyards to schoolyards. Cuff will address the lab’s projects with a focus on its community-led, post-fire initiatives. Dr. Dana Cuff, a leader in urban innovation, is a Distinguished Professor at UCLA who engages spatial justice and cultural studies of architecture as a teacher, scholar, practitioner, and activist. In 2017, after a decade of research that included a full-scale demonstration house built on the UCLA campus, Cuff co-authored the first of her several pieces of California State legislation, opening 8.1M single-family lots for secondary rental units. In 2024, she launched “Small Lots, Big Impacts,” a design-development initiative to build a new generation of dense, compact starter homes on publicly-held land. Cuff has authored numerous books, includingArchitectures of Spatial Justice(MIT Press, 2023),Urban Humanities: New Practices for Reimagining the City(MIT Press, 2020),Architects’ People(with W.R. Ellis; 1989), andArchitecture: The Story of Practice(1989).

title: Lloyd Schwartz at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Lloyd Schwartz —winner of the Pulitzer Prize for Criticism, Poet Laureate of Somerville, and the Frederick S. Troy Professor of English Emeritus at the University of Massachusetts Boston—for a discussion of his latest poetry collection, Artur Schnabel and Joseph Szigeti Play Mozart at the Frick Collection (April 4, 1948) and Other Poems. About Artur Schnabel and Joseph Szigeti Play Mozart at the Frick Collection (April 4, 1948) and Other Poems Lloyd Schwartz’s luminous new collection Artur Schnabel and Joseph Szigeti Play Mozart at the Frick Collection (April 4, 1948)and other poems reaffirms his place as one of our most keenly attentive poetic voices. With characteristic wit, intimacy, and musical acumen, these poems move fluidly between the rooms of memory and the rooms we live in, between wry horror, elegy, and celebration. The title poem “has so many planes,” said Helen Vendler. “It’s one of the most dramatic lyrics I think that it’s possible to write.” One of our most celebrated music critics tunes his verse to what Nicholas Everett tags the “idioms and nuances of American speech.” It’s like being invited into the cluttered study of a good and brilliant friend, where even the most mundane observation is shot through with a bemused heart buoyed by the nimblest of intellects. Each line twinkles at “That dark, knowing little joke,” that we are all of us connected deeply and across time by the art we love and create, and that attention itself is the highest form of devotion.

Currently studying Film Scoring at Berklee College of Music, she moves between writing for her own project, collaborating with other artists, and composing for film. Her music explores vulnerability, self-expression, and the search for connection, with the intention of making listeners feel seen, heard, and less alone. Her recent work includes the release “Better” and the placement of “The Story Never Ends” in All American . Belen is a francophone German-Filipino-American folk-adjacent singer-songwriter and multidisciplinary artist based in Boston. Known for her acoustic textures and tender songwriting, she draws on her multicultural upbringing and visual-art background to create music rooted in vulnerability and emotional storytelling. Born in Berkeley, California, and raised between a rural village in southern France and Germany, she brings a distinctive perspective to her work. She taught herself guitar at 16 before moving to Paris to study music, and now attends Berklee College of Music on a full-tuition scholarship. Her cover of “Ma Meilleure Ennemie” from Netflix’s Arcane reached over three million views across platforms, and she is currently preparing her upcoming EP, From Above . Latina Tribe is a dance fitness method primarily influenced by reggaeton and contemporary Latin music, while also incorporating elements of hip-hop, pop, and other dance styles. Since then, I have continued my training and recently earned the Senior Instructor designation, which allows me to teach across all levels of the method. Linear Salsa is a hybrid dance that comes from Mambo (a Cuban style that was popularized in the 1950’s NYC Palladium). NY Mambo is a marriage of footwork and partner-work from Cuba (Aftro-Cuban movements, Cuban Son) and the U.S. (Jazz, Swing). Salsa is a marketing term popularized in the 1970’s to commodify all Latin music and dance to a U.S. audience. Salsa is by nature transformational, multinational, and multigenerational, embodying the shared heritage of Latin music. title: David Weinberger at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes David Weinberger —researcher at Harvard metaLAB, long-time affiliate of the Harvard Berkman Klein Center, and bestselling author of Everyday Chaos —for a discussion of his new book, Beautiful Particulars: How AI’s Attention to the Smallest of Differences Is Reshaping Our Biggest Ideas. About Beautiful Particulars A fresh and eye-opening new explanation of AI—and how its focus on specifics is changing our ideas about ourselves and our world. From a Harvard researcher, philosopher, entrepreneur, former comedy writer, and bestselling author. Amid the clamor about AI, Beautiful Particulars poses a unique question: Not how does our use of AI change what we do, but how is the idea of AI already subtly yet fundamentally reshaping how we think about ourselves and our world? In clear, engaging, and even humorous prose, David Weinberger offers a new perspective on how machine learning works and how it may already be changing our basic and deepest ideas. Through lively examples, he shows that AI’s success—with all its risks and dangers—is taking us past our millennia of reliance on laws and principles by revealing what morality, free will, creativity, causality knowledge, and even reality itself look like now that we’re able to let the particulars speak their tiny truths. The author poses questions not usually asked: What does a coin look like to AI? When AI gives you evidence that the earth is round, why are its own reasons for saying that so different? Why does an AI image generator create a “selfie” of ancient Aztec warriors with broad smiles that it “believes” are historically unlikely? If AI becomes conscious but bodiless, could it still make good moral decisions? Why is the world so much better at being causal than AI could ever “understand”? How does AI show us that genuine creativity is not about a “spark” but about moments that feel right? And how can you take the temperature of a joke? title: Postpartum Movement with Nora Stephens
description: Postpartum Movement is a welcoming, supportive space to move, reconnect, and care for yourself during the postpartum journey. Move at your own pace, take breaks whenever you need, and choose what feels right for you. Babies are warmly welcome, but you do not need to bring your baby to participate. No previous movement or yoga experience is needed. All bodies, all levels, and all postpartum experiences are welcome. Come as you are. Cost: $0 – $22 Sliding Scale REGISTER HERE What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Majestic Healing Pathways™ is the foundational care model that guides all of Majestic Community Wellness’s programs. It reflects our belief that healing is a right — not a privilege — and that healing happens most sustainably when care is consistent, culturally grounded, and rooted in community. Developed in response to gaps in traditional health and wellness systems, Majestic Healing Pathways™ centers the lived experiences of Black and Brown communities who face disproportionate stress, trauma, and barriers to care. The model honors the reality that healing is not a single intervention, but a pathway built over time through breath, movement, rest, relationship, and choice. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? For more than 20 years, Nora has been teaching yoga and dance to students of all ages. She completed her 200-hour teacher training at Atmananda Yoga, and her teaching continues to be informed by years of study in Pilates, Feldenkrais, Hot Yoga, and Katonah Yoga. The births of her two children inspired her to deepen her studies in prenatal and postnatal yoga. She focused much of her teaching on supporting families and children through the various stages of development. During this time, she earned her Prenatal Yoga Certification through OM Yoga

Ballet originated in the Italian Renaissance courts around 1500 as large balls or spectacles that were performed by members of the royal court. The French king, Louis XIV, created the first academy and the positions, steps, and movements of the ballet were collected and codified. The spectacles began to be performed by artists that were trained in the academy, originally as part of an opera, and later as ballets that told a story through music, mime, and dance. Over the centuries ballet has influenced folk dance styles of many (mainly European) nations and, more recently, has been influenced by folk, modern, and contemporary forms of dance from all countries. Linear Salsa is a hybrid dance that comes from Mambo (a Cuban style that was popularized in the 1950’s NYC Palladium). NY Mambo is a marriage of footwork and partner-work from Cuba (Aftro-Cuban movements, Cuban Son) and the U.S. (Jazz, Swing). Salsa is by nature transformational, multinational, and multigenerational, embodying the shared heritage of Latin music. title: Live Blues & Roots Music Returns to Harvard Square: Wednesday Nights @ The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar
description: The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar and The Barrett Anderson Band are excited to announce a new weekly series, Blues & Roots Wednesdays , bringing live music back home to historic Harvard Square. “Cambridge, our fair city, and I share deep roots, and I’m thrilled to find a new musical home at The Sea Hag,” says Massachusetts-based singer/guitarist, Barrett Anderson. “Good music and good food are two of our most basic, fundamental needs,” he continues, “What great joy they give us. I am so happy to revel in that every Wednesday night with my dearest musical friends, and Kari and her incredible team at The Sea Hag. We go way back together, and I can’t imagine all the fun we have ahead.” Indeed, Anderson has strong connections to this scene. He remembers: “My first professional experience came when I was 15, backing up Muddy Waters’ band alums Pinetop Perkins and Bob Margolin at the original House of Blues on Winthrop Street. A few months after that I began busking, you’d often find me in Brattle Square or by the pit. This would have been mid/late 90s.” While still a teen, Anderson was a member of The Monster Mike Welch Band and Ronnie Earl & The Broadcasters (“Ronnie was my guitar hero. Then he was my teacher, then my boss. Now he’s my musical Father,” Anderson says), before eventually starting The Barrett Anderson Band in 2007. Anderson won a Boston Music Award (2013 Blues Artist of the Year), was on the Billboard charts (2020’s live album Hynoboogie spent 3 weeks on the Billboard Blues Album chart, peaking at #6), and was nominated for a Blues Music Award (2023 Band of the Year with Anthony Geraci & The Boston Blues All-Stars), all the while playing nationally, internationally, and locally in Cambridge and the greater Boston area. In addition to the musical roots, long-time locals may recognize Anderson from a decade serving tables and bartending at The Sea Hag’s sister establishment, Grendel’s Den, or from Abodeon, the mid-century modern shop started by his family. title: Hiawatha Performances and the Garden River First Nation
description: In August of 1900, several members of the Longfellow family travelled to Desbarats, Ontario, where they had been invited to attend the first performance of Henry Wadsworth Longfellow’s poem Hiawatha put on by members of the Garden River First Nation. These productions, which spread throughout Indigenous communities across Western Ontario and Northern Michigan in the years that followed, featured largely Native actors and were performed in the Anishinaabe language. Analyzing these Hiawatha performances offers a window to explore how Native people reappropriated Western representations to insist on the survival of their own peoples and traditions. This event will feature two talks about the August 1900 performance based on research done in the collections held by the Longfellow House-Washington’s Headquarters’ National Historic Site. The first, by Professor Karl Hele, will describe the context and circumstances of the performance. The second, by Professor Alan Corbiere, will look at the use of the Anishinaabe language in the performances and in the material created for the Longfellow family. Alan Corbiere , Bne wedoodemid (Ruffed Grouse clan), is an Anishinaabe from M'Chigeeng First Nation on Manitoulin Island. He is an assistant professor of history and Canada Research Chair in Indigenous History of North America at York University. His research focuses on Anishinaabe language, oral traditions, and material culture. He has published in the journals Museum Anthropology , the Algonquian Papers , and others, as well as in the edited collection Afterlives of Indigenous Archives: Essays in Honor of the Occom Circle . He has also served as the the Executive Director at the Ojibwe Cultural Foundation and the Anishinaabemowin Revitalization Program Coordinator at Lakeview School, both in M’Chigeeng First Nation. title: Infrastructure in a Time of Flux: Methods, Conditions, and Situations Symposium
description: Infrastructure in a Time of Flux: Methods, Conditions, and Situations, an exhibition curated by Rahul Mehrotra and Dan Borelli, examines how architecture, engineering, urban design, and planning respond to a world increasingly defined by environmental disruption, political instability, technological transformation, migration, and rapidly changing patterns of habitation. This symposium brings together designers, architects, humanitarian workers, and historians to reflect on the exhibition’s three themes and a case study: Case Study, Kumbh Mela:Religious pilgrimages create temporary sacred cities. Drawing work by several schools at Harvard, this interdisciplinary conversation reflects on the Kumbh Mela, one of the largest gatherings in the world, and the roads, tents, sanitation systems, ceremonial routes, and public services that support it. This panel is organized by the Lakshmi Mittal and Family South Asia Institute at Harvard University.Methods:This panel explores historic and contemporary approaches to lightweight construction: suspended, pneumatic, tensile, tensegrity, deployable, gridshell, folded, scaffolding, and spaceframe systems. Developed across different periods and disciplines, these methods use tension, air pressure, geometry, movement, modularity, and coordinated assemblies to create expansive spaces with relatively little material.Conditions:This panel brings together urbanists, economists, and political scientists to discuss the forces that continually reshape human settlements. These forces operate beyond the scale of individual buildings, transforming landscapes, redistributing resources, influencing migration, and determining where and how communities can live.Situations:Designers and researchers present contemporary examples and speculative proposals for structures that meet immediate human needs. title: Dana Mashoian Walrath at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Dana Mashoian Walrath —award-winning writer, artist, and author of the graphic memoir Aliceheimer’s —for a discussion of her haunting new graphic narrative, The Book of Genocides . About The Book of Genocides In this haunting graphic narrative, an award-winning writer, artist, and descendant of genocide survivors brings history’s darkest horrors to life, calling on us to remember, repair, and resist. The Book of Genocides is a haunting graphic narrative that compels readers to confront the most harrowing chapters of human history not as distant events but as visceral experiences. Dana Mashoian Walrath covers ten major atrocities across five centuries: the mass slaughter of the First Peoples of the Americas, the brutalization of Black Americans, the devastation of Aboriginal Australians and Torres Strait Islanders, the Armenian genocide, the Holocaust, the Cambodian killing fields, the Rwandan genocide, the Bosnian genocide, the deadly persecution of the Rohingya in Myanmar, and the genocide in Gaza. Walrath makes plain that the purpose of genocide is always a land grab, and its central apparatus is dehumanization: each chapter delves into how dehumanization operates, not just through violence but through the political and intellectual systems that enable it. The book’s unique interactive design allows readers to reshape images of victims into grotesque forms mirroring the mental mechanisms of dehumanization. With each page turn, the victims’ humanity is restored, making their suffering undeniable. The Book of Genocides is an unsettling experience, shot through with the emotional gravity of horrific events—not just historical memories but ongoing realities, painful truths that shape our world and demand our action.

title: Jake Klar with Noble Dust & Hayley Sabella
description: Live Music Template Join us at The Rockwell for a curated evening of Folk Rock and Alt-Country, celebrating Jake Klar’s album release, with special guests Noble Dust and Hayley Sabella. ABOUT JAKE KLAR: Years Go Through Me Now , a new collaborative album by singer-songwriter Jake Klar and folk-rock trio Blue Ranger, is a quiet triumph of such glimpses. In its nine songs and two interludes, I hear the motions of weathered hands, the gentle rush of country roads, the laughter of old friends and the silence of rumination — the quilt of dreams and doings we call a life. GoldFlakePaint describes Klar’s music as “An urgent meeting of folk, roots and good old rock and roll that carries with it an unbreakable spirit.” A fixture in New England’s folk scene, Klar has toured nationally, played festivals including Otis Mountain Get Down and FreshGrass, and supported the likes of Cut Worms, Antwaun Stanley, and Al Olender. Klar has spent the past decade working as a letterpress printer, art store clerk, bartender, carpenter, illustrator, graphic designer, musician (touring DIY on his own and as a member of Prewn and Hannah Mohan), live sound engineer, merch guy, and custodian. His songwriting, from the misty-eyed title track to the down-home boogie-woogie of “Driving Home Through the Country” (here recast murmurously from an earlier electric version), dwells in a rustic realm borne by his crackling voice and hearthside acoustic guitar. “That Forever” is a haunted, fragmented road-movie that emerges from its dust like a lost Basement Tapes recording, while the last-call piano ballad “Louisa” wouldn’t sound amiss on After The Gold Rush . title: Charrise Barron at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Charrise Barron —minister, a gospel artist, and Assistant Professor of Music at Harvard University—for a discussion of her new book, The Platinum Age of Gospel: The Years When Crossover Music Changed Everything. She will be joined in conversation by Jeremy D. Battle —senior pastor at The Avenue: The Historic Massachusetts Avenue & Western Avenue Baptist Church. About The Platinum Age of Gospel The story of gospel music’s chartbusting mainstream success and the accompanying shifts in Black Christian theology. From the clandestine spirituals of the enslaved—songs that voiced sorrow, hope, and an unshakeable belief in divine deliverance—to the rousing anthems of the Civil Rights era, gospel music has shaped and reflected the deepest yearnings of Black Americans striving toward freedom. During gospel’s celebrated golden age (ca. 1945–1965), the music became inseparable from the struggle for racial justice. At the same time, the genre gained unprecedented visibility in Black churches and the American mainstream. Performers such as Clara Ward, Mahalia Jackson, and Sam Cooke expanded the reach of sacred music, carrying its message across cultural and religious boundaries. Ethnomusicologist, minister, and singer Charrise Barron explores the next major era in Black gospel: the two decades between 1993 and 2013, which she calls the platinum age. In this transformative period, gospel music fully embraced the aesthetics of popular culture. Artists like Kirk Franklin and Mary Mary topped the charts, adopted contemporary styles, and reached audiences far beyond traditional church settings. Commercial success both fostered and responded to profound shifts. Influenced by Pentecostal megachurches and new theological trends, platinum-age gospel retained its spiritual resonance while largely dispensing with the golden age’s political impulses. title: The X-Tet Sounds of Italy
description: The X-tet returns with a sweeping celebration of Italian Baroque and Renaissance music , joined by GRAMMY® award-winning soprano Amanda Forsythe and viola da gamba player Cristiano Contadin . Spanning four centuries of Italy’s most treasured chamber repertoire, the ensemble brings to life virtuosic works by Vivaldi, Albinoni, Castello, and Handel alongside rarely heard gems by Maria Teresa Agnesi and Antonio Archilei. Highlights include Handel’s dramatic cantata “Armida abbandonata” and Archilei’s celestial “Dalle più alte sfere,” both featuring Forsythe’s celebrated voice, alongside instrumental showpieces for strings, theorbo, and harpsichord. The program concludes with a nod to folk tradition in the spirited Tarantella Gargano, before Colin Jacobsen’s new work , Morgantina Studies, brings the evening to a close. title: The X-Tet Sounds of Italy
description: The X-tet returns with a sweeping celebration of Italian Baroque and Renaissance music , joined by GRAMMY® award-winning soprano Amanda Forsythe and viola da gamba player Cristiano Contadin . Spanning four centuries of Italy’s most treasured chamber repertoire, the ensemble brings to life virtuosic works by Vivaldi, Albinoni, Castello, and Handel alongside rarely heard gems by Maria Teresa Agnesi and Antonio Archilei. Highlights include Handel’s dramatic cantata “Armida abbandonata” and Archilei’s celestial “Dalle più alte sfere,” both featuring Forsythe’s celebrated voice, alongside instrumental showpieces for strings, theorbo, and harpsichord. The program concludes with a nod to folk tradition in the spirited Tarantella Gargano, before Colin Jacobsen’s new work , Morgantina Studies, brings the evening to a close. Dates/Times Friday, November 13, 2026 | 7:30 PM Saturday, November 14, 2026 | 7:30 PM Estimated Run Time 90 MIN | No Intermission Location Boston Conservatory at Berklee, Seully Hall | 8 Fenway, Boston, MA 02215 Ticket Prices $30 – $70

description: Tame Your Inner Critic: A Live Book Launch & Interactive Workshop with Caitlin Green What becomes possible when you stop believing your inner critic? Join author and self-trust coach Caitlin Green for an inspiring and interactive evening celebrating the launch of her debut book, Tame Your Inner Critic . More than a traditional book launch, this experience blends storytelling, practical psychology, mindfulness, and guided reflection to help you build a more compassionate relationship with yourself. Whether your inner critic shows up as perfectionism, self-doubt, people-pleasing, or the feeling that you’re never quite enough, you’ll leave with practical tools you can begin using immediately to cultivate greater confidence, resilience, and lasting self-trust. The evening includes: ● A live author talk ● Interactive workshop exercises ● Audience Q&A ● Book signing ● Time to connect with others in a welcoming community Whether you’re navigating a career transition, healing from burnout, working toward a personal goal, or simply longing to be kinder to yourself, this evening is an invitation to stop fighting yourself—and start trusting yourself. Come for the book. Leave with a new relationship with yourself. Date: Sunday, November 15, 2026 Location: The Rockwell, Somerville, MA Doors: 4:00 PM Presentation & Workshop: 4:30 PM Book Signing & Community Mingling: Following the presentation About Caitlin Green Caitlin Green is a self-trust coach, yoga teacher, and former special educator who helps people transform self-doubt into self-trust through evidence-based psychology, mindfulness, and compassionate self-inquiry. Her work integrates science, storytelling, spirituality, and practical tools that empower people to quiet their inner critic and create lasting change. It reflects our belief that healing is a right — not a privilege — and that healing happens most sustainably when care is consistent, culturally grounded, and rooted in community. title: Shaul Magid and Zev Mishell at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Shaul Magid —Professor of Modern Judaism in Residence at Harvard Divinity School—and Zev Mishell —graduate student at Harvard University’s Committee on the Study of Religion—for a discussion of their new book, Jewish Anti-Zionism: A Historical Anthology. About Jewish Anti-Zionism A collection of texts illustrating the complex reasons why Jews have contested or rejected the Zionist ideal over more than a century. In the decades since the founding of the state of Israel in 1948, many have equated Zionism with Jewish identity—and anti-Zionism with antisemitism. Few remember now that the Zionist movement triggered passionate debate among Jews, with many expressing ambivalence or opposition to the Zionist project. In Jewish Anti-Zionism , Shaul Magid and Zev Mishell have gathered a broad selection of documents, written between the late nineteenth century and the present day, many of them newly translated into English from multiple languages, revealing the rich variety of Jewish opposition to Zionism over the decades. Following Magid and Mishell’s authoritative introduction on the history of anti-Zionism among Jews, the book features dozens of texts by Jewish writers from diverse backgrounds discussing why they reject the Zionist idea as the best option for Jewish flourishing. The documents reflect a lively debate carried out though multiple forms—personal letters, essays, speeches, manifestos, newspaper columns, and extracts from learned treatises. The authors range from scholars and other thinkers writing well before the establishment of the state of Israel to well-known contemporary voices including Peter Beinart, Noam Chomsky, Naomi Klein, and Judith Butler. Magid and Mishell preface each text with a short introduction that offers historical and ideological context.

Linear Salsa is a hybrid dance that comes from Mambo (a Cuban style that was popularized in the 1950’s NYC Palladium). title: Art + Science: Inpainting Techniques
description: Have you ever wondered what happens in our conservation labs? Taking place just outside the Straus Center in the Lightbox Gallery, this presentation will give you the chance to get up close and hands-on with a selection of tools and materials used by conservation staff. In this session, Kate Smith, senior conservator of paintings and head of the paintings lab, will talk about various philosophical approaches to restoring loss in paintings. The Straus Center for Conservation and Technical Studies is a world leader in fine arts conservation, research, and training. The center’s laboratories are where conservation, conservation science, and curatorial practice intersect, coming together to enrich the understanding of and care for the approximately 250,000 objects in the Harvard Art Museums collections.

title: Janet Rich Edwards at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Janet Rich Edwards —professor of epidemiology at Harvard University who works in the Division of Women’s Health at Brigham and Women’s Hospital—for a discussion of her national bestselling debut novel, Canticle, newly available in paperback in November 2026. About Canticle NATIONAL BESTSELLER * LONGLISTED FOR THE 2026 CAROL SHIELDS PRIZE FOR FICTION * NEW YORK TIMES EDITORS’ CHOICE * REAL SIMPLE BEST BOOKS OF 2025 * SPOTIFY BEST DEBUTS OF 2025 * GOODREADS READERS’ MOST ANTICIPATED BOOKS OF FALL A masterful debut novel following a spirited young woman’s explorations of faith, agency, and love in thirteenth-century Bruges. Aleys is sixteen years old and unusual: stubborn, bright, and prone to religious visions. She and her only friend, Finn, a young scholar, have been learning Latin together in secret—but just as she thinks their connection might become something more, everything unravels. When her father promises her in marriage to a merchant she doesn’t love, she runs away from home, finding shelter among the beguines, a fiercely independent community of religious women who refuse to answer to the Church. Among these hardworking and strong-willed women, Aleys glimpses for the first time the joys of belonging: a life of song, meaning, and friendship in the markets and along the canals of Bruges. But forces both mystical and political are at work. Illegal translations of scripture, the women’s independence, and a sudden rash of miracles all draw the attention of an ambitious bishop—and bring Aleys and those around her into ever-increasing danger, a danger that will push Aleys to a new understanding of love and sacrifice. Grounded in the little-told stories of medieval women—mystics, saints, anchoresses, and beguines—and introducing a major new talent, Canticle is a luminous work of historical fiction, vividly evoking a world on the verge of transformation.

title: Intermediate/Advanced Ballet with Dean Vollick
description: Class begins with a thorough set of exercises at the barre that last from 30 to 45 minutes. Centre practice follows, and may consist of a battement tendu exercise, a battement jeté exercise, a grand battement exercise, small and/or large adage, stationary turns, traveling turns, and petite and grand allegro enchaînement (small and big jumps). Classes are structured so that the dancer warms up their feet, legs, hips and upper body gradually. As class progresses there are more changes of weight and eventually, sudden changes of direction. Live music is provided by a pianist, that ranges from classical pieces to selections from ballet repertoire to improvisational contemporary music. Cost: $20 Single Class | $15.00 barre | 5-class package $90.00 *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. Please register in studio with the class assistant Accepted Payments: Cash, Check, Venmo What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Ballet originated in the Italian Renaissance courts around 1500 as large balls or spectacles that were performed by members of the royal court. The French king, Louis XIV, created the first academy and the positions, steps, and movements of the ballet were collected and codified. The spectacles began to be performed by artists that were trained in the academy, originally as part of an opera, and later as ballets that told a story through music, mime, and dance. Over the centuries ballet has influenced folk dance styles of many (mainly European) nations and, more recently, has been influenced by folk, modern, and contemporary forms of dance from all countries. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I had a professional dance career that spanned more than twenty years and included company work in both ballet and contemporary companies as well as dancing, choreographing, and teaching as a freelance artist.

title: Multi-Site Exhibition Tour: Alfonso Ossorio: Line and Lineage and Knowledge Is Myth: Chimeric Continuities
description: Join Ally Cirelli, curator of Alfonso Ossorio: Line and Lineage (October 23, 2026–April 11, 2027) at the Harvard Art Museums, and Danni Shen, curator of Knowledge Is Myth: Chimeric Continuities (October 1–December 13, 2026) at the Carpenter Center for the Visual Arts, for a multi-site tour of the two interconnected exhibitions. At the Harvard Art Museums exhibition, we will explore the experimental processes of modern artist Alfonso Ossorio and work by contemporary artists Enzo Camacho and Ami Lien that respond to his artistic legacy in the Philippines. Continuing to the Carpenter Center, we will view more works by Ossorio, Camacho, and Lien as well as other contemporary artists working with mythology. Throughout the tour, Cirelli and Shen will highlight the intergenerational connections made by these artists through material experimentation. Led by: Ally Cirelli, Cunningham Senior Curatorial Assistant for the Collection, Division of Modern and Contemporary Art, Harvard Art Museums Danni Shen, Senior Curatorial and Public Programs Assistant, Carpenter Center for the Visual Arts Alfonso Ossorio: Line and Lineage is made possible through the generous support of the Ossorio Fund, with additional support from the Recharge Foundation Fund for Contemporary Art. , Fund for Modern and Contemporary Art.

title: Live Blues & Roots Music Returns to Harvard Square: Wednesday Nights @ The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar
description: The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar and The Barrett Anderson Band are excited to announce a new weekly series, Blues & Roots Wednesdays , bringing live music back home to historic Harvard Square. “Cambridge, our fair city, and I share deep roots, and I’m thrilled to find a new musical home at The Sea Hag,” says Massachusetts-based singer/guitarist, Barrett Anderson. “Good music and good food are two of our most basic, fundamental needs,” he continues, “What great joy they give us. I am so happy to revel in that every Wednesday night with my dearest musical friends, and Kari and her incredible team at The Sea Hag. We go way back together, and I can’t imagine all the fun we have ahead.” Indeed, Anderson has strong connections to this scene. He remembers: “My first professional experience came when I was 15, backing up Muddy Waters’ band alums Pinetop Perkins and Bob Margolin at the original House of Blues on Winthrop Street. A few months after that I began busking, you’d often find me in Brattle Square or by the pit. This would have been mid/late 90s.” While still a teen, Anderson was a member of The Monster Mike Welch Band and Ronnie Earl & The Broadcasters (“Ronnie was my guitar hero. Then he was my teacher, then my boss. Now he’s my musical Father,” Anderson says), before eventually starting The Barrett Anderson Band in 2007. Anderson won a Boston Music Award (2013 Blues Artist of the Year), was on the Billboard charts (2020’s live album Hynoboogie spent 3 weeks on the Billboard Blues Album chart, peaking at #6), and was nominated for a Blues Music Award (2023 Band of the Year with Anthony Geraci & The Boston Blues All-Stars), all the while playing nationally, internationally, and locally in Cambridge and the greater Boston area. In addition to the musical roots, long-time locals may recognize Anderson from a decade serving tables and bartending at The Sea Hag’s sister establishment, Grendel’s Den, or from Abodeon, the mid-century modern shop started by his family. title: Dr. Omékongo Dibinga at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Dr. Omékongo Dibinga —international speaker, trilingual poet, podcast host, rapper, and professor of Intercultural Communication at American University—for a discussion of his new book, Trigger Words: How Political Language Has Made America Less Inclusive (And How to Bring Us Back Together) . About Trigger Words Trigger Words examines how language in the United States has been manipulated and politicized to sow division and dehumanization, rather than to encourage inclusion and equity. From “woke” to “DEI” to “CRT,” words that once emerged from marginalized communities to speak truth to power have been weaponized by conservative movements—especially the MAGA wing of the Republican Party—to stoke fear, shut down dialogue, and preserve systems of oppression. At the same time, however, language has been coopted by many in liberal spaces in watered-down ways that remove the overall message that was intended to be communicated by said language, such as switching terminology from “homeless” to “unhoused,” “African American” to “BIPOC,” or “Latino” to “Latinx.” This incisive and thoughtful look at how our language has been dangerously politicized by both sides of the aisle is not just a diagnosis—it is a roadmap. With experience as a university lecturer, community activist, award-winning poet, renowned professional speaker, and author ( Lies About Black People ), Dr. Omékongo Dibinga charts a path forward to reclaim and reframe these terms in their original contexts and intent. Trigger Words is an urgent and hopeful call to action that shows that healing begins when we stop simply repeating these words like ideological mantras or rejecting them out of political fear. Instead, the book invites readers to understand the deeper histories behind our most loaded social vocabulary, challenge manipulation and misuse, and foster authentic dialogue that connects rather than divides.

description: Somatic Movement is a welcoming space to slow down, reconnect with your body, and explore movement from the inside out. Through grounding, breath, gentle movement, rest, and moments of stillness, you’ll be invited to notice what your body needs and move in ways that feel supportive to you. Rather than focusing on how movement looks, this practice centers how it feels—creating space to release tension, support nervous system regulation, and build greater connection with yourself. Each class explores themes such as boundaries, self-trust, rest, joy, transition, and community. There is no right way to move and nothing to achieve. You are always encouraged to listen to your body, move at your own pace, and make the practice your own. All bodies and all levels are welcome. description: Modern Connections is a Horton based modern dance technique class taught at a pace designed for the students in the room. Class begins with sequential and consistent warm-up, continues with center phrases that are designed to promote competence and growth of proper technique. This class is designed for an Intermediate/Advanced level mover. title: Tap Level 1
description: Carrying on the tradition of Boston Tap, established by Maureen Cosgrove in 1976, these classes focus on developing technique, rhythm and musicality. Level 1 (Beginner) is geared toward those with no tap experience or those who want a refresher course. Classes are workshop format, typically 7-week sessions. Each class will build on the weeks before, but students may join at any time if space allows. Written notation for set warm-ups are available for those who are interested. New 7-week tap session 9/10 – 10/22 Cost: $20 single class | 7 week session $120 *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. Accepted Payments: Cash, Check, PayPal, Credit Card, Apple Pay (email selapbailey@gmail.com for payment information) What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Tap is an American dance form in which rhythms are audibly tapped out on the floor. It has origins in slavery and the percussive dances of West African Juba dance and Irish step dancing. It developed through minstrel shows and vaudeville in the late 19th century and emerged along with jazz in the 20th century into the art form we know today. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? Sela has been a tap teacher since 2000, taking over Maureen Cosgrove’s Boston Tap classes at the Dance Complex in 2014. While at Smith College she studied in the Five College Dance Department, performing with the Celebrations Dance Company and the UMass University Dancers. She was a founding member of the Terpsichore Ensemble in Amherst, MA and taught tap classes in Amherst and Northampton, MA before moving to Boston. title: In-Person Bellydance
description: In this class, you’ll explore earthy Egyptian, Turkish, and American style movements, dynamic combinations, and expressive choreography blending tradition and innovation. Experience the power of fiery hip-locks and shimmies, and the fluid beauty of serpentine undulations. Drawing from decades of study with master teachers and over thirty years of performance experience, Johara offers expert guidance in a supportive, inspiring environment—honoring the depth of this ancient art while inviting each student to discover their own unique style within it. Instructions: Wear comfortable dance or workout clothing that allows you to move freely. Classes are danced barefoot or in dance shoes. Students will be encouraged to acquire a veil and finger cymbals (zsagaat/ills). Cost: 7 weeks: $115 | Single Class: $20 (cash) or $23 (Venmo) *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. If you are new and want to try out the class, contact Johara for a free 1-time pass Fall Session 1: 7 Weeks – September 10 – October 22 Fall Session 2: 7 Weeks – October 29 – December 17 (no class November 26) REGISTER HERE Payment: Pay in class. Cash preferred, or Venmo Drop-ins always welcome! What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? The more authentic name for this dance form is raqs sharqi (“dance of the East”), and its roots lie in the Middle and Near East, primarily in Egypt and Turkey. This dance form was introduced to the United States and Europe at the turn of the 20th century, but it was not widely performed or taught until the 1950s and 1960s, when the belly dance craze swept across the U.S. The American cabaret style of belly dance is rooted in the legacy passed down by notable American teachers and performers, who blended Middle Eastern influences with their own innovations and movement styles drawn from diverse dance backgrounds. title: Beginner House
description: Beginner House introduces students to house music, and house dance fundamentals. No experience is required! Students will learn to understand and feel rhythm & timing patterns in house music while developing strength, fluidity and movement proficiency through basic house dance steps, grooves and functional body movements. Class is physical but fun! Come to class with an open mind and a comfortable pair of clean shoes. Cost: $20 Single Class | $95 for 5-Class Card | $185 for 10-Class Card (class cards may be used toward all Dance Complex house classes) *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. REGISTER HERE Accepted Payments: Cash, Venmo (@sean-bjerke), Paypal/Zelle (beejerks@gmail.com), Credit Card through Pre-registration What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? One of the world’s most popular music genres, “house” is an electronic dance music genre that emerged in Chicago in the late 70s/early 80s following the disco era. The term “house” was derived from The Warehouse, a Chicago club where the music was often played. Though the essence of the dance is purely freestyle, popular steps performed in NYC dance clubs were eventually recognized as “house dance foundation.” Members of NYC’s Dance Fusion were the first to teach house dance, which contributed greatly to house becoming a worldwide phenomenon. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? A master Taekwondo-ist and professional dancer, Sean began dancing in the year 2000, and was formally introduced to house dance by Boston native Ricardo Foster Jr in 2007. For years, Sean sought opportunities to learn from and train under many house dance teachers including Jardy Santiago, members of NYC’s Dance Fusion, and Edson Gonzaga who helped unlock Sean’s understanding of house music and develop his own personal dance style. title: Level 1 Salsa
description: This class starts with understanding salsa music’s rhythm and timing in addition to a brief history of the music and dance. You will learn the basic steps and partnering fundamentals. It will then move on to cover basic body movement, right turn, hesitation left turn, and cross-body lead. Learn simple turn patterns to get you out on the dance floor. Cost: $20 Single Class | $90 for 5-Class Package *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. REGISTER HERE Accepted Payments: Cash, Check, Venmo (@salsaycontroldance), PayPal, CashApp ($JohnnyGiraldo80), Zelle What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? title: Rodrigo Nunes at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Rodrigo Nunes —associate professor in philosophy at PUC-Rio, Brazil, a visiting fellow at the University of Essex, UK, and the author of Neither Vertical nor Horizontal and Organisation of the Organisationless —for a discussion of his new book, Anatomy of Disintegration: What Brazil Reveals About the Global Far Right. About Anatomy of Disintegration A leading political philosopher dissects the global far right’s appeal through the lens of Bolsonarismo, tracing its roots to the social disintegration caused by the crisis of neoliberalism and looming climate change. For four years, Jair Bolsonaro led Brazil and the popular, far-right movement that bore his name. His rise, defeat, and the chaos he left in his wake reflect patterns that are playing out in several countries, from the US to Argentina to India. In Anatomy of Disintegration , Rodrigo Nunes uses Brazil as a point of departure to make sense of why the far right is on the rise all over the world, where its appeal comes from, and explain the dystopian horizon it is moving toward. Through sharp, original analyses of the social composition of its supporters, the material and affective conditions that underpin it, and the mainstream’s inability to respond to it, Rodrigo Nunes argues that the contemporary far right is better understood not as an effort to block but as an attempt to harness and accelerate forces of social disintegration set in motion by capital and intensified by the crisis of neoliberalism.

title: Materials Lab Workshop: Casting Connections—Molds, Replicas, and Questions of Authorship
description: Join research curator Francesca Bewer for a workshop focused on art and science. We’ll explore the intimate connections between models, molds, and casts; how molds and casts have been used to produce, replicate, and preserve three-dimensional objects; and what these objects can teach us about skill, technology, and value. Working with clay, plaster, wax, alginate, and silicone putty, we’ll experiment with different processes of molding and casting. Along the way, you’ll be introduced to the scientific tools used to investigate and identify the traces of process and change. Through discussion and comparison with historical plaster casts, wax models, and other surrogates in the Harvard Art Museums collections, we’ll ask when a copy might be considered “fake,” “genuine,” or something in between, and how replicas support research, teaching, and conservation in museums today. This workshop is one of four offered this fall that explore different media through the lens of art and science. Take one or take them all! The four workshops are: Saturday, September 19: Landscape Drawing with Optical Devices Wednesday, October 7: Color Alchemy—Pigments and DIY Paint Friday, November 6: Making an Impression Friday, November 20: Casting Connections—Molds, Replicas, and Questions of Authorship

title: Brian D. Goldstein at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Brian D. Goldstein —architectural and urban historian, an associate professor and chair of the Art History Program at Swarthmore College, and author of the award-winning book The Roots of Urban Renaissance —for a discussion of his new book, Max Bond: The Life and Work of the People’s Architect . About Max Bond The first biography of a preeminent postwar architect who championed the cause of freedom through architecture and transformed Black history and modernism. J. Max Bond Jr. (1935–2009) was a civil rights activist, educator, and architect who shaped such iconic structures as the King Center for Nonviolent Social Change in Atlanta, the Smithsonian’s National Museum of African American History and Culture in Washington, DC, and the 9/11 Memorial & Museum in Manhattan. Driven by the concerns of the civil rights movement, he insisted on a practice centered on deep social engagement during years when his profession became preoccupied with celebrity and spectacle. Harvard educated and son of an eminent African American family, Bond designed housing, cultural institutions, community centers, and campuses amid an era of sweeping changes in architecture, urbanism, and American culture. He expressed an architectural vision that was democratic and inclusive, international in orientation, and celebratory of cities and their diverse residents. Yet his work has often been overlooked. Award-winning historian Brian Goldstein renders it visible. Beautifully illustrated, Max Bond is the definitive biography of one of the most important architects of our time, whose aspiration toward an architecture by and for the people was as urgent in his day as it remains in our own.

title: New on View: Community and Self-Representation in the David and Jane Shapiro Collection
description: Beginning in the late 20th century, Black artists created scenes of leisure and interior life to assert an alternative visual presence to media representations of trauma in Black life. Join Leah Yeshitila for a discussion of her installation featuring renowned artists of this period. The installation features layered representations of Black men that center community, interiority, leisure, and the rituals of everyday life, with settings ranging from D9 collegiate fraternities to barber shops. The works in the installation are drawn from a gift of David and Jane Shapiro to the Harvard Art Museums. This gallery talk is part of our New on View series, highlighting recent gallery installations and presenting new insights into recent acquisitions or old favorites. Led by: Leah Yeshitila, former Hao Family Intern in Modern and Contemporary Art

Since being established primarily as a bass player, she is diving into the songwriting indie folk role with her band of talented women, performing in the Boston area. title: Carl M. Sapers Ethics in Practice Lecture: Sylvia Lavin “Architecture After Fire”
description: This lecture, “Architecture After Fire,” argues that the rise of American architectural modernism was inseparable from the forest, not because of the use of timber, but because of modernism’s reliance on arboreal media—employing trees as information and communication systems and as metaphors. Tracking the white pine through deforestation, wildfire, and the formation of the Chicago school, this paper explores the series of substitutions, each triggered by fire, that converted environmental catastrophe into aesthetic doctrine and designated these operations as the primary function of modern architecture, artistically considered.

title: Voices Unheard
description: Voices Unheard SHOW DESCRIPTION: Voices Unheard: From the Margins to the Mic returns to Massachusetts for its seventh consecutive year, continuing its tradition of centering lived experience through story. The event features true narratives from adult storytellers who have submitted their work, sharing personal accounts of identity, origin, separation, and reunion. While participants come from a range of lived experiences—including adoption, foster care, donor conception, and unexpected family discoveries—the lineup reflects those who have chosen to step forward and share their stories this year. Together, these voices create a collective portrait of what it means to grow up without full access to one’s origins, and the ongoing search for connection, meaning, and belonging. ARTIST BIO: Lisa “LC” Coppola is a domestic DCF adoptee, writer, educator, and creator of the Voices Unheard Storytelling Program. She is the author of Voices Unheard: A Reflective Journal for Adult Adoptees and the essay Heartichoke, featured in the 2026 anthology Relative Strangers: Inheritance, Identity, and the Meaning of Kinship. Her debut novel, Monster Flower, is forthcoming from Jaded Ibis Press in Spring 2027. Kristal Parke is a talented filmmaker, producer, speaker and podcaster whose work explores identity, belonging, and resilience. A transracial adoptee from a closed adoption, her personal journey fuels her storytelling with authenticity, compassion, and truth. She creates space for unheard voices, shaping narratives that educate, challenge, inspire and heal. Majestic Healing Pathways™ is the foundational care model that guides all of Majestic Community Wellness’s programs. It reflects our belief that healing is a right — not a privilege — and that healing happens most sustainably when care is consistent, culturally grounded, and rooted in community. Developed in response to gaps in traditional health and wellness systems, Majestic Healing Pathways™ centers the lived experiences of Black and Brown communities who face disproportionate stress, trauma, and barriers to care. The model honors the reality that healing is not a single intervention, but a pathway built over time through breath, movement, rest, relationship, and choice. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? For more than 20 years, Nora has been teaching yoga and dance to students of all ages. title: Intermediate/Advanced Ballet with Dean Vollick
description: Class begins with a thorough set of exercises at the barre that last from 30 to 45 minutes. Centre practice follows, and may consist of a battement tendu exercise, a battement jeté exercise, a grand battement exercise, small and/or large adage, stationary turns, traveling turns, and petite and grand allegro enchaînement (small and big jumps). Classes are structured so that the dancer warms up their feet, legs, hips and upper body gradually. As class progresses there are more changes of weight and eventually, sudden changes of direction. Live music is provided by a pianist, that ranges from classical pieces to selections from ballet repertoire to improvisational contemporary music. Cost: $20 Single Class | $15.00 barre | 5-class package $90.00 *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. Please register in studio with the class assistant Accepted Payments: Cash, Check, Venmo What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Ballet originated in the Italian Renaissance courts around 1500 as large balls or spectacles that were performed by members of the royal court. The French king, Louis XIV, created the first academy and the positions, steps, and movements of the ballet were collected and codified. The spectacles began to be performed by artists that were trained in the academy, originally as part of an opera, and later as ballets that told a story through music, mime, and dance. Over the centuries ballet has influenced folk dance styles of many (mainly European) nations and, more recently, has been influenced by folk, modern, and contemporary forms of dance from all countries. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I had a professional dance career that spanned more than twenty years and included company work in both ballet and contemporary companies as well as dancing, choreographing, and teaching as a freelance artist.

title: Live Blues & Roots Music Returns to Harvard Square: Wednesday Nights @ The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar
description: The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar and The Barrett Anderson Band are excited to announce a new weekly series, Blues & Roots Wednesdays , bringing live music back home to historic Harvard Square. “Cambridge, our fair city, and I share deep roots, and I’m thrilled to find a new musical home at The Sea Hag,” says Massachusetts-based singer/guitarist, Barrett Anderson. “Good music and good food are two of our most basic, fundamental needs,” he continues, “What great joy they give us. I am so happy to revel in that every Wednesday night with my dearest musical friends, and Kari and her incredible team at The Sea Hag. We go way back together, and I can’t imagine all the fun we have ahead.” Indeed, Anderson has strong connections to this scene. He remembers: “My first professional experience came when I was 15, backing up Muddy Waters’ band alums Pinetop Perkins and Bob Margolin at the original House of Blues on Winthrop Street. A few months after that I began busking, you’d often find me in Brattle Square or by the pit. This would have been mid/late 90s.” While still a teen, Anderson was a member of The Monster Mike Welch Band and Ronnie Earl & The Broadcasters (“Ronnie was my guitar hero. Then he was my teacher, then my boss. Now he’s my musical Father,” Anderson says), before eventually starting The Barrett Anderson Band in 2007. Anderson won a Boston Music Award (2013 Blues Artist of the Year), was on the Billboard charts (2020’s live album Hynoboogie spent 3 weeks on the Billboard Blues Album chart, peaking at #6), and was nominated for a Blues Music Award (2023 Band of the Year with Anthony Geraci & The Boston Blues All-Stars), all the while playing nationally, internationally, and locally in Cambridge and the greater Boston area. In addition to the musical roots, long-time locals may recognize Anderson from a decade serving tables and bartending at The Sea Hag’s sister establishment, Grendel’s Den, or from Abodeon, the mid-century modern shop started by his family. description: Classes will be broken into 5 sections at Level 1. New sessions start the first Monday of every odd month. No partner required. *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. *Students who purchase a membership for the Dance Complex will get that $25 taken off their 10 class new student rate, bringing it down to $85. Cost: $23 Single Class | $85 for 5-Class Package | $130 for 10-Class Package | $110 for new student 10-class package Cash, Venmo (@Brendan-Folan), Zelle (bjfoley21@gmail.com) REGISTRATION: Not Required, Drop-Ins Welcome What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Linear Salsa is a hybrid dance that comes from Mambo (a Cuban style that was popularized in the 1950’s NYC Palladium). NY Mambo is a marriage of footwork and partner-work from Cuba (Aftro-Cuban movements, Cuban Son) and the U.S. (Jazz, Swing). Salsa is a marketing term popularized in the 1970’s to commodify all Latin music and dance to a U.S. audience. Circular Salsa primarily comes from the Cuban dance Casino, which itself originates from Cuban Son. Salsa is by nature transformational, multinational, and multigenerational, embodying the shared heritage of Latin music. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I was the assistant teacher of this class for over 2 years under Ricardo Contreras. Level 1 (Beginner) is geared toward those with no tap experience or those who want a refresher course. Classes are workshop format, typically 7-week sessions. Each class will build on the weeks before, but students may join at any time if space allows. Written notation for set warm-ups are available for those who are interested. Tap is an American dance form in which rhythms are audibly tapped out on the floor. It has origins in slavery and the percussive dances of West African Juba dance and Irish step dancing. It developed through minstrel shows and vaudeville in the late 19th century and emerged along with jazz in the 20th century into the art form we know today. title: Intermediate Advanced Modern Connections

title: In-Person Bellydance
description: In this class, you’ll explore earthy Egyptian, Turkish, and American style movements, dynamic combinations, and expressive choreography blending tradition and innovation. Experience the power of fiery hip-locks and shimmies, and the fluid beauty of serpentine undulations. Drawing from decades of study with master teachers and over thirty years of performance experience, Johara offers expert guidance in a supportive, inspiring environment—honoring the depth of this ancient art while inviting each student to discover their own unique style within it. Instructions: Wear comfortable dance or workout clothing that allows you to move freely. Classes are danced barefoot or in dance shoes. Students will be encouraged to acquire a veil and finger cymbals (zsagaat/ills). The more authentic name for this dance form is raqs sharqi (“dance of the East”), and its roots lie in the Middle and Near East, primarily in Egypt and Turkey. This dance form was introduced to the United States and Europe at the turn of the 20th century, but it was not widely performed or taught until the 1950s and 1960s, when the belly dance craze swept across the U.S. The American cabaret style of belly dance is rooted in the legacy passed down by notable American teachers and performers, who blended Middle Eastern influences with their own innovations and movement styles drawn from diverse dance backgrounds. One of the world’s most popular music genres, “house” is an electronic dance music genre that emerged in Chicago in the late 70s/early 80s following the disco era. The term “house” was derived from The Warehouse, a Chicago club where the music was often played. Though the essence of the dance is purely freestyle, popular steps performed in NYC dance clubs were eventually recognized as “house dance foundation.” Members of NYC’s Dance Fusion were the first to teach house dance, which contributed greatly to house becoming a worldwide phenomenon. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? A master Taekwondo-ist and professional dancer, Sean began dancing in the year 2000, and was formally introduced to house dance by Boston native Ricardo Foster Jr in 2007. For years, Sean sought opportunities to learn from and train under many house dance teachers including Jardy Santiago, members of NYC’s Dance Fusion, and Edson Gonzaga who helped unlock Sean’s understanding of house music and develop his own personal dance style. Latina Tribe is a dance fitness method primarily influenced by reggaeton and contemporary Latin music, while also incorporating elements of hip-hop, pop, and other dance styles. Reggaeton developed through a blend of Caribbean and Latin American influences, with roots in Panama and Puerto Rico and strong connections to reggae en español, dancehall, and hip-hop. Latina Tribe is a dance fitness method primarily influenced by reggaeton and contemporary Latin music, while also incorporating elements of hip-hop, pop, and other dance styles. Reggaeton developed through a blend of Caribbean and Latin American influences, with roots in Panama and Puerto Rico and strong connections to reggae en español, dancehall, and hip-hop. Since then, I have continued my training and recently earned the Senior Instructor designation, which allows me to teach across all levels of the method. Majestic Healing Pathways™ is the foundational care model that guides all of Majestic Community Wellness’s programs. It reflects our belief that healing is a right — not a privilege — and that healing happens most sustainably when care is consistent, culturally grounded, and rooted in community. Developed in response to gaps in traditional health and wellness systems, Majestic Healing Pathways™ centers the lived experiences of Black and Brown communities who face disproportionate stress, trauma, and barriers to care. The model honors the reality that healing is not a single intervention, but a pathway built over time through breath, movement, rest, relationship, and choice. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? For more than 20 years, Nora has been teaching yoga and dance to students of all ages. She completed her 200-hour teacher training at Atmananda Yoga, and her teaching continues to be informed by years of study in Pilates, Feldenkrais, Hot Yoga, and Katonah Yoga. The births of her two children inspired her to deepen her studies in prenatal and postnatal yoga. She focused much of her teaching on supporting families and children through the various stages of development. During this time, she earned her Prenatal Yoga Certification through OM Yoga

title: Intermediate/Advanced Ballet with Dean Vollick
description: Class begins with a thorough set of exercises at the barre that last from 30 to 45 minutes. Centre practice follows, and may consist of a battement tendu exercise, a battement jeté exercise, a grand battement exercise, small and/or large adage, stationary turns, traveling turns, and petite and grand allegro enchaînement (small and big jumps). Classes are structured so that the dancer warms up their feet, legs, hips and upper body gradually. As class progresses there are more changes of weight and eventually, sudden changes of direction. Live music is provided by a pianist, that ranges from classical pieces to selections from ballet repertoire to improvisational contemporary music. Cost: $20 Single Class | $15.00 barre | 5-class package $90.00 *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. Please register in studio with the class assistant Accepted Payments: Cash, Check, Venmo What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Ballet originated in the Italian Renaissance courts around 1500 as large balls or spectacles that were performed by members of the royal court. The French king, Louis XIV, created the first academy and the positions, steps, and movements of the ballet were collected and codified. The spectacles began to be performed by artists that were trained in the academy, originally as part of an opera, and later as ballets that told a story through music, mime, and dance. Over the centuries ballet has influenced folk dance styles of many (mainly European) nations and, more recently, has been influenced by folk, modern, and contemporary forms of dance from all countries. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I had a professional dance career that spanned more than twenty years and included company work in both ballet and contemporary companies as well as dancing, choreographing, and teaching as a freelance artist.

M. W. Turner, John Constable, Gustave Courbet, Edouard Manet, Berthe Morisot, Paul Cézanne, and Vincent van Gogh, among many others. The exhibition is on view from September 18, 2026 to January 17, 2027. This event is part of In Conversation, a series of evening programs that feature local and international curators, artists, scholars, and more. Running from September through April, these events highlight our temporary exhibitions, permanent collections, and a range of creative voices. Funding for the exhibition and related programming was provided by the Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Support Fund, the Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Support Fund for the Study of Dutch Drawing, the Melvin R. Seiden and Janine Luke Fund for Publications and Exhibitions, and the M. Victor Leventritt Lecture Series Endowment Fund. Linear Salsa is a hybrid dance that comes from Mambo (a Cuban style that was popularized in the 1950’s NYC Palladium). title: Hooly J Chan Full Band and Jessye DeSilva
description: Hooly J Chan Full Band and Jessye DeSilva Through music and puppetry Hooly J Chan and full band tell a love story for earthlings… transmitted from extraterrestrials… In this story we witness an earthling getting taken up into the beyond and coming back down again… A consciousness altering experience. The high of coming in contact with the aliens… of coming in contact with ourselves… of coming in contact with our earthly impact while we’re here… With special guest Jessye DeSilva Hooly J Chan is a story teller, singer songwriter and puppeteer based in the South Coast of Massachusetts. Co-founder of The Wicked Queer Puppet Theater, hooly creates musical and visual art to expand our imagination of what is possible. Contact High is hoolys 4th full length album. Their band includes woodwinds, strings, bass, guitars, and drums and together they take audience on a journey into the ethers! Contact High is a story about coming in deeper contact with ourselves, each other, our Earth and the beyond… Jessye DeSilva seamlessly blends theatrical pop elements with traditional folk and roots music to form her piano-driven alt-americana sound. She infuses hope into songs about religious alienation, mental health struggles, and societal injustice to create a uniquely queer and unholy ruckus. Jessye’s latest album Glitter Up the Dark was produced by Aaron Lee Tasjan and incorporates Eighties pop and Nineties alternative flourishes to the stately Americana and country-rock sounds of 2023’s Renovations and 2022 debut Landscapes, which earned her a nomination for Americana Artist of the Year at the 2022 Boston Music Awards. No Depression says “Comparisons to Elton John and Brandi Carlile are easy — DeSilva clearly takes a page from these idols, anchoring [her] songs in pop melody juggernauts, gauzy textures, and vocal bravado.” Nashville Scene named her a 2023 Artist To Watch, saying “DeSilva could inject new life into a genre that could definitely use a little more pretzel logic.” SOCIAL

Though the essence of the dance is purely freestyle, popular steps performed in NYC dance clubs were eventually recognized as “house dance foundation.” Members of NYC’s Dance Fusion were the first to teach house dance, which contributed greatly to house becoming a worldwide phenomenon. title: In-Person Bellydance
description: In this class, you’ll explore earthy Egyptian, Turkish, and American style movements, dynamic combinations, and expressive choreography blending tradition and innovation. Experience the power of fiery hip-locks and shimmies, and the fluid beauty of serpentine undulations. Drawing from decades of study with master teachers and over thirty years of performance experience, Johara offers expert guidance in a supportive, inspiring environment—honoring the depth of this ancient art while inviting each student to discover their own unique style within it. The more authentic name for this dance form is raqs sharqi (“dance of the East”), and its roots lie in the Middle and Near East, primarily in Egypt and Turkey. This dance form was introduced to the United States and Europe at the turn of the 20th century, but it was not widely performed or taught until the 1950s and 1960s, when the belly dance craze swept across the U.S. The American cabaret style of belly dance is rooted in the legacy passed down by notable American teachers and performers, who blended Middle Eastern influences with their own innovations and movement styles drawn from diverse dance backgrounds. title: Michael Bravata: "The Montcalms" Release Show
description: Michael Bravata: “The Montcalms” Release Show Celebrating the release of his 2026 album The Montcalms , Michael Bravata will perform the record live in its entirety, backed by a full band, including a strings section. Musicians who helped record the album will join him on stage to recreate its fully acoustic, all-natural instrumentation at The Rockwell. Michael Bravata is a Boston-based experimental guitarist and composer who has spent his career creating a catalog of evocative and immersive avant-garde pieces. Born in Texas, Michael spent his formative years in the vibrant indie music scenes of Dallas and Austin. While pursuing a degree at UTA, Michael wrote and created music driven through post-rock and drone genres. Over the past decade, Michael’s insatiable appetite for artistic exploration and growth has led him to the experimental world of ambient landscapes. This shift marked an evolution in his music, reflecting a deeper examination of acoustic textures and immersive atmospheres. title: Christy Scott Cashman at Harvard Book Store
description: Harvard Book Store welcomes Christy Scott Cashman —best-selling and award-winning author, actress, producer, and the founder of the nonprofit YouthINK—for a discussion of her new novel, What Happened in Beulah . About What Happened in Beulah A teenage girl uncovers the dark secrets of her Smoky Mountain town while searching for a missing classmate in this gripping coming-of-age mystery perfect for fans of Where the Crawdads Sing . Nestled in the foothills of the Smoky Mountains, Beulah has always seemed steady—rooted in tradition, shaped by generations, and slow to change. But in 1986, the ground has shifted, and no one feels that more than fifteen-year-old Barrett Childress Owens. Between her parents’ unraveling marriage and a school full of kids she can’t connect with, she feels invisible in her own hometown. When Lacy Gunderson, the captivating new girl everyone is curious about, suddenly vanishes, the town’s calm surface fractures. Search parties comb the woods. A police investigation begins. Rumors multiply. Families close ranks. And Barrett begins to sense how much the adults around her choose not to say. As Beulah clings to its usual rituals—including the annual Miss Kudzu pageant, which has shaped local girlhood for decades—Barrett is forced to navigate a community where loss lingers in the air and secrets are carefully kept. Her journey through the uncertainty reshapes her understanding of friendships, family, and the complex place she calls home. A rich coming-of-age story with a pulse of mystery and a budding romance, What Happened in Beulah explores the fault lines of a small town and the courage it takes to face the truths people would rather bury.

Each move is built into easy-to-follow choreography, making it both exciting and accessible. Expect a lot of fun, great music, and a vibe that keeps you moving and smiling the whole time! Cost: $25 Single Class *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. REGISTER HERE Accepted Payments: Venmo, PayPal, CashApp, Credit Card – refer to website What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Hip hop – is a street dance form that derived from clubs and house parties in the 80’s. It has its rich and soulful roots in the African American Culture. It’s characterized by bounces, rocks vibin’ all intertwined with grooves that help you understand the attitudes and soul of African American culture. This class is a beginner choreography class. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? With over 36 years of performance experience, Carl has shared the stage with recording artists like Gladys Knight, Ray Charles, Neil Young, and Sir Elton John, and has coached A-list celebrities such as Brooke Shields, Brendan Fraser, and Ken Jeong. As a talent agent, he represented talent that worked on projects for Michael Jackson, Chris Brown, Beyonce, and “In the Heights” on Broadway to name a few. His book, “Speak Confidently On Camera: Avoid These 12 Critical Mistakes And Be The Coach You Were Meant To Be,” is an Amazon best seller. Serving on worship teams since the mid-1990s, Carl has honed his and others skills both for on stage and camera.
